delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe low stakes, no ongoing plot and humor from understated reactions to magic (ANN Spring 2017 Manga Guide; The Manga Critic).
delivery.note: The idea that magic is in everything is never preached; it comes from the pace and the art of ordinary days.

personified.ideology: Witchcraft as gentle craft and care for nature

76258.dominant: Pagan/occult (witchcraft as benign craft), Communitarianism, Environmentalism (seasons and nature).

126559.heading: Fool Night
126559.label: From summaries
126559.life_message: A society that buys the lives of its poorest people to keep everyone else breathing is unjust, and even a life with two years left finds meaning in compassion, in helping others, and in refusing to treat anyone as a thing.

content.framing: Condemned (murders and terror shown as products of injustice)

delivery.evidence: Both the pro- and anti-transfloration sides are shown as self-interested; VIZ's vol. 5 blurb says the heroes question whether they are on the right side (VIZ).
delivery.note: The ethical question is posed openly in blurbs and plot, but answered through characters' fates rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: Compassion and usefulness in a short life

32895.heading: Forest of Piano (Piano no Mori)
32895.label: From summaries
32895.life_message: Talent grows through hard work, good teachers and loyal friends, and where you come from does not decide who you can become.

content.framing: Mixed: the district shown with sympathy; Kai's relationship with Sae presented as true love
Condemned when used as a slur

delivery.evidence: Ajino and the competition judges state ideas about music openly, but Shuhei's father and the strict judges are given reasons (Japanese Wikipedia); the story's view comes through Kai's results.
delivery.note: The message about class and talent is clear but carried by the competition plot rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: play your own sound; talent plus work

32895.dominant: Expressive individualism (Kai's own sound), Classical virtue ethics (discipline and excellence), Communitarianism (the district, the street band, friends), Patriotism / nationalism (critiqued in the competition's national bias).

85417.heading: Forget Me Not
85417.label: From summaries
85417.life_message: The people we hurt while growing up stay with us; facing those memories honestly is how we learn to love better, even if we cannot undo what we did.

content.framing: Neutral; peer cruelty condemned through regret

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: The lesson comes through Serizawa's narration and regret rather than lectures (ANN; AIPT); the women are drawn as types (ANN).
delivery.note: The frame story (the mystery caller) turns each flashback into a question: is this the woman I wronged?

85417.dominant: Existentialism (responsibility for one's past choices) and Classical virtue ethics (character formed by failure and growth).

69139.heading: Fort of Apocalypse
69139.label: From summaries
69139.life_message: Boys the world has written off can become humanity's last line of defense when they trust each other, stand by each other and are willing to give themselves up for others.

content.framing: Neutral (survival horror); cult and prison cruelty condemned

delivery.evidence: No source comments on preaching; synopses and TV Tropes show the outlook carried by plot and backstories. The cult's beliefs are given only as madness and deception, and Thompson notes the shonen habit of clear good and bad guys.
delivery.note: Its view that outcasts can be heroes is carried by action and backstory, not speeches; the cult is drawn as a villain without a real case.

personified.ideology: worship of the Bokor; faith as a tool of power

69139.dominant: Pragmatism, Communitarianism, Might makes right (explored), Secular humanism.

82435.heading: Fragments of Horror
82435.label: From summaries
82435.life_message: No single model of a good life: betrayal, obsession and morbid curiosity draw people into horror, faithless men pay for it, and only one story finds tenderness, in letting the dead say goodbye.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: The Guardian notes Ito avoids being political; McCulloch sees a recurring theme of faithless men but doubts it is sincere (via Wikipedia; TCJ).
delivery.note: Each story is built to shock or unsettle; any message about fidelity or grief is implied, not argued.

82435.dominant: Pagan/occult (demons, spirits, curses), Absurdism, Feminism (as critics read it), Nihilism.

85402.heading: Fragtime
85402.label: From summaries
85402.life_message: Real closeness means dropping the masks you wear to please people and letting someone see and choose the real you; the story also shows a romance that begins with a violation of privacy and asks the reader to accept the apology.

content.framing: Mixed: peeping and frozen-time intimacy framed as romance; the teacher's touching left ambiguous
Mixed: peeping framed as the meet-cute; later choices shown with consequences

delivery.evidence: The climax has Moritani confront Murakami about her mask and declare her love (Wikipedia); Murakami's flipbook of roles states the theme. No character questions the peeping premise beyond Moritani's apology (CBR).
delivery.note: The authenticity theme is carried by the climax rather than lectures; the consent questions raised by critics are not addressed inside the story.

personified.ideology: Withdrawal from people, then honest love

35806.heading: Franken Fran
35806.label: From summaries
35806.life_message: Life is to be saved at any cost, yet getting exactly what you crave can turn you into a monster: the satire turns vanity, greed and cruelty back on the people who indulge them.

content.framing: Neutral (black comedy) for surgery and mutation; killings by Veronica and Gavrill shown as action; cruelty to the weak punished
Mixed: sexual abuse condemned and punished; nudity mostly clinical; crude sexual jokes for shock

delivery.evidence: Episodic monkey's-paw stories let consequences speak; Veronica's opposite creed is given real sympathy (fan wiki), and no character lectures the reader.
delivery.note: Each case lets vanity and greed produce grotesque results, so the satire works through outcomes rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: Every living form is good; life must be saved at any cost
A painless death over a painful life

35806.dominant: Transhumanism (critiqued), Absurdism, Naturalism, Duty ethics (Fran's never-kill rule).

35911.heading: Freezing
35911.label: From summaries
35911.life_message: Patient, faithful love between partners can heal deep trauma, and people treated as disposable weapons deserve to be treated as people; strength means never giving up.

content.framing: Neutral (battle action); cruelty by villains condemned
Mixed: abuse and assault condemned by the plot; fan service and sexual humiliation framed as entertainment
Mixed: student drinking as comedy; drug experiments condemned

delivery.evidence: Elizabeth and Charles argue openly about justice and sacrifice (vol. 12); the Chevalier are drawn as cold villains; the romance and fan service carry most chapters (Wikipedia; fan wiki).
delivery.note: The critique of exploitation is stated in the E-Pandora arcs, but the series rarely examines its own sexual content.

personified.ideology: Duty and sacrifice for the system

35911.dominant: Transhumanism (engineered girls as weapons, critiqued), Might makes right (rank by force), Authoritarianism (the Chevalier, critiqued), Utilitarianism (girls sacrificed for the war, critiqued).

118586.heading: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End
118586.label: From summaries
118586.life_message: Time with people is short and precious: pay attention to them while you can, because the kindness of those we lose goes on living in the people it changed.

content.framing: Neutral; killing demons framed as justified defense
Neutral; played as a gentle character flaw

delivery.evidence: Sequential Tart (via Wikipedia) calls it "serene and contemplative"; ANN's Eisenbeis praises "deep thematic explorations of human nature" (via Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The message is shown through episodes and flashbacks, not speeches; Eisen's and Heiter's views on death are both given space, but demons get no point of view of their own.

personified.ideology: Learning to value fleeting human bonds
Faith held with humor; belief in heaven
Stoic acceptance; the dead return to dust
A demon trying to understand malice

118586.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Existentialism (meaning in a short life).

116495.heading: From Leveling Up the Hero to Leveling Up a Nation
116495.label: From summaries
116495.life_message: Patiently developing other people's abilities builds lasting strength, for a party or a whole land; being let go is a new beginning, not an ending.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: The premise states the idea (train people and the land grows strong; BookWalker vol. 1); the hero who dismissed Eiga is good-natured rather than a strawman (Dengeki Online).
delivery.note: A management fantasy whose message is carried by the plot of building and training rather than by speeches (to verify).

personified.ideology: The hero who outgrew his teacher

145675.heading: From Old Country Bumpkin to Master Swordsman: My Hotshot Disciples Are All Grown Up Now, and They Won't Leave Me Alone
145675.label: From summaries
145675.life_message: Patient, honest work and humility bear fruit in other people: a good teacher's legacy is the people he helped grow, and even a modest man has to learn to accept that his work matters.

content.framing: Duels endorsed as skill; cruelty and treachery condemned
Mixed: harem comedy among adults; nothing explicit reported

delivery.evidence: Beryl's worth is stated by every student he meets; the arrogant vice commander is shown up in one duel. Antagonists are thinly drawn in sources opened.
delivery.note: The message is carried by repetition (each reunion confirms Beryl's value) and light comedy rather than argument.

personified.character: The bishop of the Church of Sphene

145675.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (humility, mastery), Communitarianism (found family), Confucian ethics (teacher and disciple).

113171.heading: From Overshadowed to Overpowered: Second Reincarnation of a Talentless Sage
113171.label: From summaries
113171.life_message: Steady effort and knowledge can outlast a lack of talent, and great power should be used to free and protect the weak rather than to lord it over them.

content.framing: Mixed: the hero's overwhelming force celebrated; villains' cruelty condemned
Mixed: sexual threats condemned; fan service and the slave-girl setup treated neutrally

delivery.evidence: Villains are snobs and abusers who gloat (Orcott, Edwards, Abe, ep. 2-9); a MyAnimeList reviewer notes that good characters are drawn attractive and bad ones ugly. Ephtal states his encouragement to Anastasia directly (ep. 4, 9).
delivery.note: The values (effort, protecting the weak) are carried by the plot and a few direct speeches; the opposing view (rank by birth and aptitude) is given no fair case.

personified.ideology: Effort and knowledge beat talent; power protects
Worth by lineage and inborn aptitude

113171.dominant: Strength rules (explored), Classical virtue ethics (effort and mastery), Expressive individualism, Liberalism (freedom from slavery).

123687.heading: From the Red Fog
123687.label: From summaries
123687.life_message: It holds up no model life: it shows how a child raised in abuse and isolation becomes a killer, and asks, without a clear answer, whether connection can still reach him.

content.framing: Neutral: told from a killer's view; many victims are innocent
Shown as abuse; off the page

delivery.evidence: Will voices the humane view and is killed; later characters give speeches about family and love that some fan reviewers found preachy (MyAnimeList); critics say the story mostly shows cruelty without judging it (ANN; But Why Tho).
delivery.note: The story shows a killer's path from the inside and leaves readers to weigh nature against nurture.

personified.ideology: Killing as the only way to feel

123687.dominant: Nihilism, Naturalism (nature versus nurture), Might makes right, Existentialism.

85848.heading: Fukushuu Kyoushitsu (Revenge Classroom)
85848.label: From summaries
85848.life_message: Revenge does not heal a bullied child: it spreads harm to friends and bystanders, turns the victim into someone worse, and leaves her broken, while the adults who should have protected children look away.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; the heroine's violence escalates
Condemned as abuse; used by the heroine as a weapon
Mixed: the methods are shown to work, then to destroy

delivery.evidence: The message is carried by events, not lectures: deaths of the innocent, Ayana's growing coldness and her end. Ren's plea that she live is the only voice against revenge (Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The story invites sympathy with Ayana at the start and withdraws it by stages; readers who stop early may take it as a revenge fantasy.

personified.ideology: Vengeance as justice, extended to bystanders

85848.dominant: Might makes right (power reversal), Nihilism (the mastermind's last word), Existentialism (a life given to one purpose).

30008.heading: Full Moon (Full Moon o Sagashite)
30008.label: From summaries
30008.life_message: Life is a gift worth choosing even in grief; love for the living and the dead can coexist, and dreams are pursued by deciding to live.

content.framing: Mixed: young love sympathetic; the adult affair shown as unhappy and ended
Played for comedy, later shown as a coping habit
Shown with consequences (regret, and the choice to live)

delivery.evidence: Takuto's own regret is the argument that persuades Mitsuki to live (fan wiki); each shinigami's backstory restates the cost of suicide; antagonists (Fuzuki, Izumi, Sheldan) get sympathetic histories (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The message is spoken by characters at key moments, but most of it is carried by backstories and the plot's outcome rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: regret for suicide; love that protects
music as the thing that takes loved ones
death must be taken on schedule

30008.dominant: Expressive individualism (her dream), Existentialism (choosing life in the face of death), Pagan/occult (a Japanese death-spirit world), Feel-good faith (a gentle heaven and a guardian soul).

30025.heading: Fullmetal Alchemist
30025.label: From summaries
30025.life_message: A good life is lived within human limits. You accept loss, own your mistakes, work for what you get, give more than you take, and protect others instead of trying to become a god.

delivery.evidence: Arakawa set out to put social issues in the story and presents the Ishval war from many viewpoints (Wikipedia; The Mary Sue). Villains get motives (Hohenheim's history, Scar's grief); Father's pride is the clearest moral.
delivery.note: The themes are stated by characters (equivalent exchange, the all-is-one teaching, the meaning of family) but carried mostly by plot and consequences rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: Equivalent exchange, then humility and love beyond exchange

30025.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Authoritarianism (critiqued), Transhumanism (critiqued), Duty ethics, Secular humanism (humble), Communitarianism.

120067.heading: Futari Escape
120067.label: From summaries
120067.life_message: When adult life grinds you down, small escapes shared with someone who loves you (a drive, a meal, a trip) can carry you through.

delivery.evidence: Each chapter simply shows an escape; no character argues for hard work over rest, and the editor is treated kindly (blurbs; reviews).
delivery.note: The message lives in the mood; the romance is shown, not argued.

120067.dominant: Hedonism (gentle), Expressive individualism, Progressivism; iyashikei comfort.

86244.heading: Futaribeya: A Room for Two
86244.label: From summaries
86244.life_message: A shared everyday life built on small kindnesses and on accepting each other's differences is a quiet, lasting happiness; the person who fits your life can be the one who is simply always there.

delivery.evidence: A 4-koma gag format with no stated thesis; Okazu describes long stretches with no romance at all, and Manga Bookshelf says readers who do not want the romance can easily read past it.
delivery.note: The relationship is carried by gestures (one bed, matching mugs, gifts, a shared apartment) rather than words.

86244.dominant: Communitarianism (home and friends), Expressive individualism (living at one's own pace), Progressivism (implied same-sex couple, explored).

160651.heading: Futarijime Romantic
160651.label: From summaries
160651.life_message: Real love grows from knowing a person as they are rather than from a fairy-tale script; the "wrong" person can turn out to be the right one.

delivery.evidence: The theme is in the setup itself (the right name, the wrong boy); Tajima's realism is shown as partly right.
delivery.note: A light rom-com; the message comes through the romance, not speeches.

160651.dominant: Expressive individualism (gentle), with a romance about character over fate.

30584.heading: Future Diary
30584.label: From summaries
30584.life_message: No power, not even a god's, can undo death or force a happy ending; obsession and the hunger to control the future destroy people, and love proves itself by letting the other one live.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; killing is how the game is won
Mixed: abuse and assault condemned; the teen leads' sexual relationship presented as romance
Mixed: stalking played as devotion, then shown as destructive

delivery.evidence: Most characters are given motives (Kurusu's son, Kamado's orphans, Minene's lost parents); the cult and Bacchus are drawn as pure exploiters; the meaning is left to the ending rather than stated.
delivery.note: The story rarely comments on itself; its verdict comes from consequences, as almost every path ends in death.

personified.ideology: Survival, then power to undo death

30584.dominant: Might makes right (critiqued), Nihilism, Existentialism (fate versus choice), Transhumanism

85216.heading: Fuuka
85216.label: From summaries
85216.life_message: Grief does not have to end a shared dream: by keeping faith with a lost friend's music, and by letting new people in, you can carry love forward.

content.framing: Neutral; the death is shown as tragedy
Neutral (fan service as comedy); romance endorsed

delivery.evidence: The message is carried by band and romance drama (AniList Band, Tragedy); no critic comments on preachiness. Makoto's father is the only figure who argues the other side, and he is shown unsympathetically (TV Tropes).
delivery.note: Grief and loyalty are shown through what the band does after ch. 36, not argued in speeches.

personified.ideology: Keeping promises and a shared dream
Parental control over career and marriage

85216.dominant: Communitarianism (the band as family), Expressive individualism (music as self-expression).

86864.heading: Gabriel Dropout
86864.label: From summaries
86864.life_message: Labels do not decide character: a lazy angel can still be kind when it counts, a "demon" can be the most dependable friend, and good friends keep pulling each other back toward decency.

content.framing: Played for comedy; voyeurism shown as creepy and rebuffed
Played for comedy, mildly corrected by friends

delivery.evidence: An episodic gag comedy; no reviewer cites a message beyond the role reversal (ANN Manga Guide; Anime Feminist).
delivery.note: The role reversal is the joke; the series does not argue for any view.

personified.ideology: Abandoned duty for comfort and play
Goodness regardless of one's assigned side

86864.dominant: Hedonism, Moralistic therapeutic deism, Absurdism, Consumerism, Communitarianism.

144946.heading: Gachiakuta
144946.label: From summaries
144946.life_message: Nothing and no one is trash: things and people others throw away still have worth, and a good life cares for them, protects them and refuses to throw anyone away.

content.framing: Mixed: cruelty condemned; battle action heroic

delivery.evidence: Rudo states the theme (nothing is trash) and Regto's dying words state the goal; the Sphere's elite and accusers are drawn flatly, but Raiders and Cleaners get backstories.
delivery.note: The message is visual as well as spoken: Vital Instruments are made of cherished junk, and graffiti carries meaning (Wikipedia).

personified.ideology: Value in the discarded; revenge on the unjust
Objects and people have souls; change the world
Save the discarded; protect, don't destroy

144946.dominant: Critical theory (class and waste), Environmentalism, Communitarianism, Consumerism (critiqued).

30320.heading: Gakuen Alice
30320.label: From summaries
30320.life_message: Friendship, kindness and courage can stand up to adults and institutions that use children, and love is worth giving everything for.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; abuse of children condemned

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: comic gags and child romance played lightly; abuse and assault condemned; a teacher-student romance with a minor endorsed

delivery.evidence: The principal is a pure villain, but Persona, Luna and Goshima are given reasons and redemption; the story states friendship as the key (Wikipedia plot summary).
delivery.note: The anti-abuse message is carried by plot, not lectures; the problematic romances are presented sympathetically without comment.

30320.dominant: Communitarianism (friendship), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued: the academy), Might makes right (critiqued: the principal).

98112.heading: Gal Gohan
98112.label: From summaries
98112.life_message: Someone who believes in you can turn failure into a calling, and love between a teacher and a student should wait until they can meet as equals.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy (fan service); the romance is deferred until after graduation (to verify)
Played as comedy; the teacher resists (to verify)

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe a light comedy driven by Miku's teasing and Yabe's flustered resistance (Manga Bookshelf; Otaku USA); the case against a teacher-student romance is voiced mainly through Yabe's hesitation and school rules (Fujiwara, vol. 3).
delivery.note: The message about effort and waiting is carried by comedy and fan service rather than stated.

personified.ideology: self-expression and pursuit of what you want

98112.dominant: Expressive individualism (gyaru self-expression and pursuit), Classical virtue ethics (effort and growth), Hedonism (food and fan service).

194302.heading: #Gal x Gal Yuri
194302.label: From summaries
194302.life_message: Love can start on a whim between best friends and grow into a lasting commitment when both partners are openly, happily glad of each other.

content.framing: Endorsed (the romance); sexual talk played as comedy

delivery.evidence: No one in the story objects to the relationship (Okazu); acceptance is shown, never argued.
delivery.note: A light comedy that assumes its view rather than stating it.

179484.heading: GALAXIAS
179484.label: From summaries
179484.life_message: Curiosity is worth the risk: going out to know the world and yourself, with friends at your side, is better than living safe and small, even when a powerful state wants you gone.

content.framing: Mixed: battle action as thrilling; cruelty by villains condemned

179484.dominant: Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Expressive individualism, Might makes right, Existentialism (my own framing).

delivery.evidence: Comic Natalie reads the theme of curiosity through the characters rather than speeches; villains like Chalk are cartoonishly cruel, while Antares is given moments of humanity (fan wiki).
delivery.note: A classic adventure whose message, go out and know the world, is carried by action and wonder, not lectures.

personified.ideology: Protective love that keeps a child safe and small
Loyal, ruthless service to the state

138380.heading: Gals Can’t Be Kind to Otaku!?
138380.label: From summaries
138380.life_message: People are more than their labels: friendship and love grow when you stop hiding what you enjoy and stop judging others by their clique.

content.framing: Neutral: flirtation and teasing; nothing explicit reported

delivery.evidence: Critics describe a light comedy whose point (people are more than one thing) comes through the characters, not speeches (ANN; Anime Feminist).
delivery.note: Acceptance across cliques is shown in each small episode rather than stated; no character argues for the school caste.

138380.dominant: Expressive individualism (stop hiding who you are), Communitarianism (friendship and family), Consumerism (fandom as bond).

44582.heading: Gamaran
44582.label: From summaries
44582.life_message: Strength earned through hard training and shared with loyal comrades is worth pursuing, but strength that cuts every bond destroys itself; the son who could take revenge on his father chooses instead to surpass him in his own way.

content.framing: Endorsed as martial excellence; cruelty and massacre condemned
Lewdness played for laughs and punished
Mixed: a drunken master shown with respect; a combat drug shown with heavy costs

delivery.evidence: Characters state their creeds before duels (Jinsuke, Muraku, the 47th Corps); reviewers say the later arcs become dialogue-heavy (MyAnimeList, mastertek, Jimbo11). Antagonists get backstories, and many are respected in death (Baian, Midou; Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The message is carried by fights and by the final choice, not by lectures.

personified.ideology: Strength through training; loyalty; finally mercy
Abuse as a way to forge strength

44582.dominant: Bushido / honor code, Might makes right (explored and finally refused), Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism.

33572.heading: Gambling Apocalypse: Kaiji
33572.label: From summaries
33572.life_message: The rich and powerful rig the game against the desperate, so trust, nerve and clear thinking are the only defenses; but greed and the urge to win big can ruin even someone who sees through the system.

content.frequency: Occasional, heavy in the late arcs
content.framing: Shown with consequences; cruelty of the organizers condemned

delivery.evidence: E-Card is an open allegory of Emperor, Citizen and Slave (Wikipedia); a talkative, grandiose narrator explains the stakes with wild metaphors (Daryl Surat of Otaku USA, via Wikipedia); Tonegawa and Hyodo deliver lectures that Fukumoto calls cruel truths.
delivery.note: The class message is stated in the games' design and in villains' speeches, but the villains are given strong arguments about personal responsibility, so the story does not simply preach one side. Whether the English edition's narration reads as heavy-handed was not checked.

personified.ideology: Desperate underdog relying on wits and, slowly, on trust
Winners deserve to win; debtors are to blame for themselves
The rich may use the poor for amusement
Self-sacrifice for family and a friend

33572.dominant: Strength rules (critiqued), Marxism (class struggle explored), Existentialism, Pragmatism.

54903.heading: GANGSTA.
54903.label: From summaries
54903.life_message: In a city that treats some people as disposable, loyalty to the few who stand by you, and refusing to treat anyone as less than human, keeps you alive and decent, but the cost is high and the world does not change easily.

content.framing: Neutral (killing as work); cruelty and massacre condemned
Mixed: forced prostitution and abuse condemned; adult sex work treated as a job

delivery.evidence: The anti-discrimination theme is carried by the setting (tags, the Three Laws, massacres) rather than speeches; Otaku USA calls the stories simplified revenge fantasy; anti-Twilight villains get little inner life in sources opened.
delivery.note: The message is shown through who suffers and who protects whom; the heroes are not idealized, and the creator has spoken about the theme only outside the book (Real Sound).

personified.ideology: Survive and protect your own; refuse contempt
Charm and loyalty over a hidden contempt for all
Pragmatic power that uses the weak

54903.dominant: Might makes right (the city's law), Critical theory (discrimination against an engineered underclass), Communitarianism (found family of outcasts), Bushido / honor code (the Guild's code).

107910.heading: Gannibal
107910.label: From summaries
107910.life_message: A closed community's silence lets terrible evil go on; standing against it takes courage and costs dearly, a child's compassion can reach even a monster, and the evil is not easily ended.

content.framing: Condemned (cannibalism, child sacrifice, clan murder); police force shown as necessary but costly
Condemned (abuse); a recurring joke about the wife's figure

delivery.evidence: The clan's reasons are given a history (Gin's sacrifice and survival, vol. 10-11), and Keisuke and Shirogane get sympathy, but the practice itself is never defended by the story.
delivery.note: The message is carried by suspense and revelation, not speeches; the ending withholds a clean moral.

personified.ideology: Law, justice and a protective rage
Duty to the house versus conscience
Power through fear, sex and sacrifice
Villagers who hate and fear the Gotos

107910.dominant: Traditionalism (critiqued), Authoritarianism (clan rule, critiqued), Strength rules (critiqued), Communitarianism (critiqued).

86637.heading: Gantz:G
86637.label: From summaries
86637.life_message: In a cruel and arbitrary world, survival and meaning come from working together, protecting each other and refusing to give up on the people you love, rather than from rivalry or revenge.

delivery.evidence: Action-first death game; ANN says personal issues (bullying, abuse, stalking) are handled at surface level.
delivery.note: Themes of teamwork and loyalty come through the missions, not through speeches.

86637.dominant: Existentialism (life and death in an absurd game), Communitarianism (the team), Nihilism (explored: meaningless deaths).

30564.heading: Gantz
30564.label: From summaries
30564.life_message: A good life is found in caring for particular people (a girlfriend, a little brother, a friend) and protecting them, even in a universe that shows no sign of caring back; selfishness and cruelty are common and ugly, and self-giving love is rare and costly.

content.framing: Neutral to shown with consequences; massacres condemned
Mixed: sexual assault shown as vile; fan service and casual sex not framed critically

delivery.evidence: Most themes come through events; the final arc states its cosmology through a long speech by the being behind Gantz (v36). A MyAnimeList reviewer finds no meaningful philosophy; Yokogao Magazine reads it as a study of the human condition.
delivery.note: Oku says he uses grotesque and erotic scenes, surprise and humor to keep readers engaged (Gigazine, 2016), so the message is often secondary to the spectacle.

personified.ideology: Meaning found through love and loyalty
Humanity is insignificant; order without care

30564.dominant: Existentialism, Nihilism (explored), Naturalism, Secular humanism, Absurdism.

71733.heading: Gate: Where the JSDF Fought
71733.label: From summaries
71733.life_message: A disciplined, restrained army serving a peace-loving nation can protect the weak, free the enslaved and win the trust of strangers, while rulers who govern by cruelty and conquest destroy themselves.

content.framing: Mixed: JSDF firepower shown as decisive and heroic; Imperial atrocities condemned
Mixed: rape and sexual slavery condemned; fan service and harem comedy endorsed

delivery.evidence: THEM: opposition politicians and foreign leaders are caricatures and the JSDF near flawless; ANN's Silverman calls it possibly too political and open to reading as glorifying the military; Martin finds the manga follows the JSDF's official self-image.
delivery.note: The case for the JSDF is made openly through Diet hearings, diplomats' speeches (ch. 30) and battle outcomes; the novels' web version was more nationalistic still (Wikipedia).

personified.ideology: Apostle of a war god; killing judged by its reasons

71733.dominant: Patriotism / nationalism, Authoritarianism (critiqued), Liberalism (rights and consent), Strength rules (explored).

45578.heading: GE: Good Ending
45578.label: From summaries
45578.life_message: Love worth having is honest: stop calculating, face your own feelings and the other person's wounds, and choose each other freely; manipulation, pressure and exposing someone's private life do lasting harm.

content.framing: Condemned (abuse and assault); slaps played as drama
Mixed: teen sex treated as a normal step; exploitation and pressure condemned

delivery.evidence: No source addresses delivery directly; MyAnimeList reviewers describe melodrama and many misunderstandings rather than lectures.
delivery.note: The honesty-over-strategy message is carried by the relationships and their breakups.

45578.dominant: Expressive individualism, Classical virtue ethics (growth in honesty and courage), Hedonism (explored).

30348.heading: Genshiken
30348.label: From summaries
30348.life_message: Accepting yourself and what you love without shame, and finding friends who accept you, is how you grow up; growing up also means moving on.

content.framing: Mixed: erotic fan material treated as a normal hobby; sex kept offscreen

delivery.evidence: The series argues for self-acceptance through slow change in Sasahara and Ogiue, not speeches; Saki's non-otaku view is given full dignity and she is never converted (Wikipedia; Ogiue Maniax). ANN praises its subtle art of poking fun at fans.
delivery.note: The message is mostly shown in small scenes over four years; Kio's attention to background detail is praised (Wikipedia).

personified.ideology: Accept what you love without shame
Shame and self-hatred about one's desires
Otaku pride; fear of growing up

30348.dominant: Expressive individualism (self-acceptance), Consumerism (fan culture, celebrated and satirized), Communitarianism (the club as found family), Postmodernism (meta-parody of otaku media).

85197.heading: Giganto Maxia
85197.label: From summaries
85197.life_message: Strength is for protecting and sparing, not destroying: a true warrior fights so that both sides can walk away, and stands with a threatened people against an empire that would wipe them out.

content.framing: Mixed: arena and giant battles shown as heroic; killing and genocide condemned
Played as embarrassed comedy; not judged

delivery.evidence: Otaku USA: the morality "strives for compassionate black & white, not grimdark gray"; the Empire is a faceless aggressor, and Ogun's distrust is shown as understandable.
delivery.note: The message is carried by how Delos fights rather than by speeches; Prome's narration explains the world more than it argues.

personified.ideology: Strength in the service of mercy
Cool analysis and duty to her contractor
Tribal pride; outsiders are the Empire's dogs

85197.dominant: Might makes right (critiqued), Classical virtue ethics, Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Pacifism / nonviolence (explored).

30044.heading: Gin Tama
30044.label: From summaries
30044.life_message: Keep your own soul straight and protect the people within arm's reach: whatever rulers, invaders or fate do, loyalty to friends and a personal code are what make someone a true samurai.

content.frequency: Frequent in serious arcs; comic violence constant
content.framing: Mixed: comic violence unjudged; killing in war and revenge shown with cost
Mixed: laziness and stalking played as comedy; loyalty endorsed

content.frequency: Recurring (in story) and outside the book

delivery.evidence: Sorachi describes the series as gently portraying a loser's life and a likeable humanity (Wikipedia, Hideaki Sorachi); serious arcs state the code through Gintoki's actions between gag chapters.
delivery.note: The personal code is shown more than preached; villains like Takasugi and Kamui get their reasons, though tyrants such as Housen are flat.

personified.ideology: A personal code of protecting one's own
Destroy the world that took his teacher
Duty and discipline to the group

30044.dominant: Communitarianism (found family), Bushido / honor code (a personal code), Absurdism and Postmodernism (parody), Classical virtue ethics.

33102.heading: Girl Friends
33102.label: From summaries
33102.life_message: Honest love is worth the risk: two friends afraid of losing each other find that telling the truth about their feelings brings them closer, and the story treats their love as real and serious.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers note conflict comes from misunderstanding rather than prejudice (Lesbrary) and that the relationship is treated seriously without speeches (ANN; Okazu).
delivery.note: Its message about honesty in love is carried by the slow build of the two girls' relationship, not stated.

33102.dominant: Expressive individualism (being true to one's feelings), Progressivism (same-sex love treated seriously), Communitarianism (the friend group).

116266.heading: Girlfriend, Girlfriend
116266.label: From summaries
116266.life_message: Love offered openly, honestly and with everyone's agreement can work even when it breaks the usual rules; the series keeps asking whether a boy who loves several girls at once can be forgiven, and answers yes.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy; coercive advances played for laughs and finally rewarded

delivery.evidence: Naoya states his principles loudly and often; the creator frames the whole series as testing whether two-timing can be forgiven (Comic Space, 2021); Shino's monogamy argument is voiced, then dissolved by her own feelings.
delivery.note: A self-aware parody that nonetheless argues for its premise and gives it a happy ending.

116266.dominant: Expressive individualism (choosing your own relationship form), Progressivism (non-monogamy normalized), Postmodernism (self-aware harem parody), Duty ethics (Naoya's rules of honesty).

128448.heading: Glasses With a Chance of Delinquent
128448.label: From summaries
128448.life_message: People are more than their past or their looks; a person who wants to change deserves trust and a second chance, and love and friendship help them keep changing.

content.framing: Mixed: fighting as a habit to outgrow, but fights to protect are endorsed

delivery.evidence: Blurbs show the message carried by events: Ichikura keeps or breaks his promise not to fight, classmates react to his past (vol. 4), Momose questions his methods (vol. 8). Rival delinquents are given personalities and some become friends (Yachiyo). No review on delivery could be opened.
delivery.note: The second-chance theme rides on romantic comedy and rival-of-the-arc plots rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: fear of the past turning into trust

128448.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (self-control, keeping promises), Expressive individualism (more than appearances), Might makes right (critiqued), Communitarianism.

86607.heading: Gleipnir
86607.label: From summaries
86607.life_message: Two broken teenagers who let each other in can carry what neither could carry alone: sharing guilt, memory and danger ("the two of us are one") is what lets them face the monsters and the truth about their past, though the bond begins in coercion and is sealed in killing.

content.framing: Neutral; killing by the heroes shown as necessary but frightening

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Played as dark fan service and psychosexual metaphor; the opening undressing is framed as shameful
Shown with consequences; the suicide vow is framed as devotion
Mixed: coercion shown as frightening but effective

delivery.evidence: No character lectures; the theme of shared guilt is stated in titles (ch. 5, "The Two of Us Are One") and in Shuichi's resolve after the Madoka defeat (Japanese Wikipedia). Villains such as Kaito and Elena are given tragic backstories rather than drawn as strawmen.
delivery.note: The message is carried by the bond and the suit metaphor; ANN's Jones reads the intimacy of the leads as the real subject, more than the coin game.

personified.ideology: Truth and survival at any cost
Strength rules; loyalty to his own

86607.dominant: Existentialism (identity and memory), Might makes right (the coin game), Nihilism (critiqued in Kaito), Utilitarianism (Clair's methods).

107234.heading: Go For It Again, Nakamura!
107234.label: From summaries
107234.life_message: Loving someone means wanting their happiness even when it hurts, and a true friendship is worth keeping while you wait and grow.

content.framing: Gay crush shown sympathetically; a student's one-sided crush on a teacher played for comedy; no sexual activity

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe episodic gag chapters with no stated lessons (Boys Love Library; M.J. Lyons); acceptance of Nakamura is assumed rather than argued.
delivery.note: Courage, loyalty and acceptance are carried by comedy; the teacher subplot is presented as a joke rather than examined.

86549.heading: Go For It, Nakamura!
86549.label: From summaries
86549.life_message: Small, brave steps toward someone you care about are worth the embarrassment, and a real friendship is a happy ending in itself.

content.framing: Gay crush shown sympathetically; no sexual activity

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe a gag comedy in which the gay lead is never the punchline (The OASG) and the message comes only through Nakamura's attempts (Manga Bookshelf; Anime Feminist).
delivery.note: Courage and acceptance are carried by comedy, with no stated lessons.

personified.ideology: Shy, sincere love and growing courage

127564.heading: Go! Go! Loser Ranger!
127564.label: From summaries
127564.life_message: Heroes and villains can be labels written by whoever controls the show; real justice means seeing through the performance, refusing to treat anyone as a disposable extra, and choosing your side by what is right rather than by your costume.

content.framing: Mixed: action played for thrills and comedy; cruelty by heroes condemned

delivery.evidence: The Keepers are given backstories and mixed motives (Aoshima's orphanage, Chidori's grief), but the Red Keeper is a near-cartoon tyrant; the theme of staged heroism is shown through plot reveals rather than speeches.
delivery.note: The message emerges through twists that keep moving the line between hero and villain; D's inner monologue states his changing loyalties outright.

personified.ideology: Rebellion of the disposable; choosing one's own side
Rule by fear and a manufactured hero myth
Revenge without empathy, then the worth of every life

127564.dominant: Critical theory (heroism as manufactured power), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Postmodernism (who is the villain?), Might makes right (critiqued).

87020.heading: Go with the Clouds, North-by-Northwest
87020.label: From summaries
87020.life_message: Love for family must not blind you to the truth: patient, honest attention to people and places, the way Kei listens to his car and to Iceland itself, is how you find out what is real, even when the truth is about someone you love.

content.framing: Played as comedy (groping, walk-ins); romance gentle
Sympathetic to Kei; Michitaka's pathology condemned

delivery.evidence: Kei's wrong assumption about Jon is corrected without a lecture (v3); Michitaka's guilt emerges slowly through evidence, not statements.
delivery.note: The series lets landscapes and small moments carry its feeling; its mystery advances in fits and starts.

87020.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (loyalty versus truth), Pragmatism (detective work), Environmentalism (reverence for Iceland).

100117.heading: Goblin Slayer Side Story: Year One
100117.label: From summaries
100117.life_message: Grief turned into a single purpose can protect the people no one else will help, but a life given wholly to killing needs a home, friends and a future to stay human.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; goblin-killing presented as grim necessary work
Mixed: sexual violence condemned as the goblins' evil, but drawn salaciously (ANN); fan service of young women

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers find the protagonist undeveloped rather than preachy; other characters (Arc Mage, Young Warrior, the examiner) question his single-mindedness, but goblins are never given a point of view.
delivery.note: The message is shown through his choices and their results; it is never argued aloud.

100117.dominant: Pragmatism, Classical virtue ethics, Stoicism, Utilitarianism.

31470.heading: Gon
31470.label: From summaries
31470.life_message: Life in the wild is hungry, rough and funny; strength is at its best when it shares the food and stands up for the small, even in a hero who is mostly out for himself.

content.framing: Neutral (the food chain shown as nature); bullying predators humbled
Played as comedy, mostly without consequence for Gon

delivery.evidence: Told without words; reviewers praise universal visual storytelling (Wikipedia; Otaku USA); any message is inferred from events.
delivery.note: There is no stated message; the moral pattern (bullies humbled, the young defended) emerges from episodes and is often undercut by Gon's own antics.

87415.heading: Goodbye, Dragon Life
87415.label: From summaries
87415.life_message: A life is made worth living by the people you love and the ordinary work you share with them; even the mightiest being finds his reason to live in friendship, family and a home.

content.framing: Endorsed (defense of the village and forest); villains' cruelty condemned

delivery.evidence: Dolan states his reason to live to Kalavis (anime ep. 12); prejudice is voiced by the militia captain and a priestess who change their minds (anime ep. 2), and by an official who turns out fair.
delivery.note: The value of humble community life is carried by the premise and by quiet scenes; the story states its theme once at the climax rather than lecturing.

personified.ideology: Humble work, friendship and protection; strength hidden
An outsider seeking love and a place
Self-worship of beauty at any cost
Battle as the meaning of life

87415.dominant: Communitarianism (village and forest peoples), Classical virtue ethics (humility, courage, loyalty), Pagan/occult (a real fantasy pantheon and nature spirits), Existentialism (a reason to live chosen in a second life).

146983.heading: Goodbye, Eri
146983.label: From summaries
146983.life_message: Grief, love and memory are all things we partly make up, and that is not a lie but a way to go on: a person can choose to live, and remembering someone at their best, while knowing it is edited, can be an act of love.

content.framing: Shown with consequences (deaths); explosions played as dark comedy
Shown with consequences; both suicide plans abandoned

delivery.evidence: Reviewers praise its ambiguity and film-like framing; ANN says some may find the manipulation confusing or pretentious; none call it preachy.
delivery.note: Its ideas about grief, memory and fiction come through framing and ambiguous events rather than stated morals, and objections to the first film get a sympathetic voice.

personified.ideology: Facing loss through art and edited memory
Fiction as a way to be remembered
Self-image and control before her child
Respect for the dead and the truth about them

146983.dominant: Postmodernism (fiction and reality), Existentialism (choosing to live), Expressive individualism (art as self), Absurdism (the explosion gag).

111970.heading: Goodbye, My Rose Garden
111970.label: From summaries
111970.life_message: Love does not have to hide or end in despair: leaving a beautiful but confining life to live honestly with the person you love is worth what it costs, and the wish to die can give way to a life chosen together.

delivery.evidence: The rose-garden metaphor and the Wilde reference carry the theme (Wikipedia; ANN); Edward is kind, not a cartoon, but the story clearly sides with the lovers (Anime Feminist).
delivery.note: Victorian norms are shown as the source of Alice's despair; the message is carried by character and symbol rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: The world, not Alice, needs fixing

111970.dominant: Expressive individualism, Feminism, Progressivism, Traditionalism (critiqued), Liberalism (consent in marriage).

34632.heading: Goodnight Punpun
34632.label: From summaries
34632.life_message: The series does not promote a single picture of a good life. It shows how neglect, abuse and isolation damage children, and it suggests that ordinary survival, with work and a few human ties, is what is left after the dream of rescue through one perfect love fails.

delivery.evidence: Asano (ANN interview, 2018) says the work offers no answers, only questions.
delivery.note: The series avoids stated morals and leaves most of its verdicts open.

personified.ideology: Frank friendship and creative work as a reason to go on

34632.dominant: Existentialism, Nihilism (explored, not affirmed), Absurdism, Postmodernism, Buddhist ideas by echo.

30958.heading: Goth
30958.label: From summaries
30958.life_message: The story offers no model of a good life; it studies two teenagers drawn to death and asks what separates a person fascinated by darkness from one who acts on it, and its answer is unsettling: very little.

content.framing: Neutral (shown coldly, neither celebrated nor condemned)
Explored, not resolved; one reviewer says it romanticizes mental illness

delivery.evidence: No message is stated; Experiments in Manga notes the story pauses to let images sink in and reveals how abnormal characters are. In the manga postscript Otsuichi points readers to the novel's other stories and outcomes (Publishers Weekly).
delivery.note: No moral framework is offered; readers must judge the narrator themselves.

30958.dominant: Nihilism, Existentialism (a detached narrator and a girl drawn to death).

87395.heading: Grand Blue Dreaming
87395.label: From summaries
87395.life_message: A good life is shared with loyal friends who laugh, drink and dive together; embarrassment passes, the sea is worth the effort, and you stand by your friends and family when it counts.

content.framing: Endorsed (played for laughs); occasional comic consequences

delivery.evidence: No lectures; the story never stops to judge the drinking, and Screenwise notes no counter-perspective. Characters who object (Aina, Iori at first) are swept along for laughs.
delivery.note: The message about friendship and the sea is carried by situations, not speeches; the rare serious moments (Palau, the diving scenes) speak for themselves.

personified.ideology: Reluctant joiner who comes to love the group and the sea

85457.heading: GTO: Paradise Lost
85457.label: From summaries
85457.life_message: A real teacher puts himself between young people and the adults who would use them, even at the cost of his job and his freedom; fame and power do not excuse exploiting the young.

content.framing: Mixed: Onizuka's fists and stunts endorsed as comedy and justice; yakuza, cult and warden violence condemned

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: sexual exploitation of students condemned and stopped; adult casual sex and the hero's lust played as comedy; one coerced encounter turned into romance
Mixed: smoking unremarked; illegal drugs condemned
Mixed: endorsed as heroism, then paid for with prison

delivery.evidence: Villains (a 'pervert producer', a fortune-teller with 'psychoelectric waves', a warden) are cartoonish; Onizuka states his lessons in confrontations at the end of each arc (chapter titles such as A Teacher's Dignity, ch. 75).
delivery.note: Each arc builds to a showdown and a short speech, but most of the message is carried by action and comedy rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: Industry power that owns the young
Fraudulent spirituality that preys on grief

85457.dominant: Pragmatism (whatever protects the students), Consumerism (critiqued: the fame industry), Hedonism (explored), Communitarianism (the class and the old gang).

30445.heading: GTO: The Early Years - Shonan Junai Gumi
30445.label: From summaries
30445.life_message: Real manhood is loyalty to your friends and standing up for the weak, not reputation or conquests; a legend built on fighting has to be laid down for a young man to grow up.

content.framing: Endorsed (gang fights as heroic); cruelty and killing condemned
Mixed: sexual comedy endorsed; sexual violence condemned but often quickly forgiven

delivery.evidence: Villains (Akutsu, Nanno, the traffickers) are mostly drawn as monsters to be beaten; some rivals (Saejima, Kamata, Fumiya, Joey) are given backstories and redeemed.
delivery.note: The "manliness" theme is acted out in fights and loyalty rather than stated, and the ending's doubt about the legend is quiet.

30445.dominant: Bushido / honor code (a delinquent code of loyalty and manliness), Communitarianism (the gang as family), Strength rules (explored), Hedonism.

30649.heading: Gunslinger Girl
30649.label: From summaries
30649.life_message: Children turned into weapons keep their humanity and their need to love, but using them, however good the cause, destroys them and corrupts the adults who do it; what survives is love, memory and a hope handed to the next generation.

content.framing: Mixed: counterterrorism action shown as effective; its cost to the children shown as tragic
Abuse condemned; the girls' attachments to adult handlers presented as tender and tragic

delivery.evidence: The story seldom states a verdict; it shows the cost through deaths and memory loss. Terrorists and the assassin Pinocchio are given motives and backstories (vols. 3-5).
delivery.note: A quiet, melancholy story whose judgment comes through what happens to the girls, which leaves room for very different readings.

personified.ideology: Love and devotion as reason to live

31319.heading: Gunsmith Cats
31319.label: From summaries
31319.life_message: Skill, nerve and loyalty to the people who share your home carry you through a violent world, and a good shot can stop evil without killing; the story also treats a teenage girl's sexual relationship with an adult as a romance.

content.framing: Mixed: action played for thrills; murder, rape and drug crime condemned

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Endorsed (the adult-minor relationship is presented as romance); assault and Goldie's sexual abuse condemned
Condemned (drug trade as the villains' weapon)

delivery.evidence: No speeches; the values are carried by action and character. Villains like Goldie are given motives (a criminal order without harmful drugs), and some characters voice objections to the May-Ken age gap (ANN; TV Tropes).
delivery.note: An action series whose message lives in what it rewards (skill, loyalty, restraint) and what it treats as normal (May's relationship), not in what it says.

personified.ideology: Skill and justice by her own code
A professional's code: honor the deal

31319.dominant: Pragmatism, Libertarianism (armed self-reliance), Expressive individualism, Hedonism (explored).

109017.heading: Gushing over Magical Girls
109017.label: From summaries
109017.life_message: It treats a shy girl's discovery that she enjoys dominating and humiliating the heroines she adores as comic self-discovery; later chapters add a struggle to master that urge (her split into "Reason" and "Lust") rather than be ruled by it.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: No speeches; the view is carried by genre parody and by Utena's delight. ANN's Christopher Farris notes a hopeful turn in episode 12, where Utena respects the heroines' resilience.
delivery.note: The story frames Utena's urge as part of who she is; later arcs make self-control, not shame, the goal.

personified.ideology: Indulging the urge to dominate; self-acceptance

109017.dominant: Hedonism (desire indulged), Expressive individualism (the true self), Postmodernism (genre parody).

30909.heading: Gyo
30909.label: From summaries
30909.life_message: Weapons and obsessions people create can outlive them and come back to destroy everyone; against a horror no one can stop, love lingers and a few keep searching for a cure.

delivery.evidence: No speeches about war or science; the warning sits in the backstory (ch. 6-7) and the imagery. Ito said the idea came from wanting a shark that could also attack on land, after Jaws (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: Gyo is built to disturb rather than to argue; any message is carried by image and consequence.

30909.dominant: Naturalism (biological horror), Absurdism (a grotesque, half-comic premise), Nihilism (cosmic dread).

49087.heading: Haganai: I Don't Have Many Friends
49087.label: From summaries
49087.life_message: You may already have the friends you think you lack; admitting it, and being honest about your feelings, is harder and better than hiding behind jokes.

delivery.evidence: The message (the club are already friends) is carried by situations and by Rika's late outburst, not lectures; Kimlinger (ANN, via Wikipedia) says the message stays the same throughout.
delivery.note: The series is self-aware about harem clichés (Gaffney calls it meta), but uses them anyway.

personified.ideology: Avoidance to keep the group together
Distrust and loyalty to the past

49087.dominant: Communitarianism (friendship as found family), Expressive individualism (misfits as themselves), Postmodernism (meta, otaku parody); Hedonism in the fan service.

65243.heading: Haikyu!!
65243.label: From summaries
65243.life_message: Find what you love and give it everything, but you cannot fly alone: each person's strengths, and weaknesses, matter only inside a team. Losing is part of the game and a reason to grow, not the end of your worth.

delivery.evidence: Coaches and players state the lessons, but rival teams are drawn with their own philosophies and are respected, and Karasuno loses.
delivery.note: Messages about effort and teamwork are spoken openly by coaches and players, inside match drama rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: Learning and caring as a teacher

65243.dominant: Communitarianism (the team), Classical virtue ethics (character built by practice), Pragmatism, Confucian ethics (respect for seniors and teachers).

201773.heading: Haimiya Is Scary Cute
201773.label: From summaries
201773.life_message: People are more than their reputations, and quiet kindness can draw a lonely person out; friendship grows when someone chooses to see you.

delivery.evidence: The message (do not judge by looks) is carried by the gap between Haimiya's reputation and her behavior; no review on delivery was found (to verify).
delivery.note: A gentle comedy; kindness is shown, not argued.

30057.heading: Hana-Kimi: For You in Full Blossom
30057.label: From summaries
30057.life_message: Wholehearted, loyal encouragement can help someone you love recover what they lost, and true friends protect each other; but a life built on a disguise cannot last, and in the end you have to be seen as who you are.

content.framing: Protective violence endorsed; cheating and bullying condemned
Mixed: chaste central romance; predators condemned; orientation jokes as comedy
Shown with consequences; healing through support
Shown with consequences in the end

delivery.evidence: Lessons come through comedy and romance; characters who dislike gay people (Mizuki's brother) are played for laughs; the predators are flat villains.
delivery.note: A long, episodic shojo comedy with serious arcs about grief and family.

personified.ideology: Overprotective brother who dislikes gay men

30057.dominant: Expressive individualism (living by one's heart), Communitarianism (the dorm as family), Progressivism (gender and orientation explored).

111168.heading: Handsome Girl and Sheltered Girl
111168.label: From summaries
111168.life_message: Love is for the person, not the category; honesty, even when it is frightening, is what lets a relationship last.

delivery.evidence: A romantic comedy; acceptance is shown through Satomi's reaction rather than argued, and social acceptance is discussed in only a chapter or two (AniList review).
delivery.note: The message rides on the reveal and its aftermath; no character argues against the couple in sources opened.

personified.ideology: Authentic self-presentation; love worth being honest for
Love the person, whatever the category

111168.dominant: Expressive individualism (live and love as yourself), Progressivism (same-sex love and gender presentation affirmed), Duty ethics (the obligation to tell the truth).

104730.heading: Handyman Saitou in Another World
104730.label: From summaries
104730.life_message: Ordinary, practical skills have real worth, and being needed and thanked by friends can heal a person who believed he was worthless.

content.framing: Mixed: sexual comedy played for laughs, unjudged; romance sincere

delivery.evidence: Siliconera describes efficient short stories that build on each other; ANN says the work-and-appreciation thread gives the party real camaraderie; no reviewer calls it preachy.
delivery.note: The value of humble work is shown through small episodes, not speeches; the contempt of Saitou's old life is sketched briefly.

104730.dominant: Pragmatism (the worth of practical skill), Communitarianism (found family), Classical virtue ethics (humility, diligence).

37760.heading: Hanma Baki (Baki: Son of Ogre)
37760.label: From summaries
37760.life_message: Strength is the measure of a man, and the son who grows strong enough to stand against his father finally wins that father's recognition.

content.framing: Condemned by onlookers within the story, but the attacker is later treated as a sympathetic fighter and never punished

delivery.evidence: Characters openly declare strength the measure of worth; Baki's relational strength is set against Yujiro's crushing strength (fan wiki, Baki Hanma page).
delivery.note: Yujiro is monstrous yet admired, and the climax ends in mutual recognition rather than condemnation.

personified.ideology: Strength through bonds and fighting spirit

37760.dominant: Might makes right (explored, central), Naturalism (Pickle), Bushido / honor code (code among fighters).

116809.heading: Happy Harem Making with the Mightiest Orc!
116809.label: From summaries
116809.life_message: Become strong and work hard, and you can win the partners and the life you want; the story's lighter counterweight is that Olc will not take a woman who is not willing.

content.framing: Endorsed (sexual comedy; consent respected per reviewers)

delivery.evidence: The mother states the thesis outright: the weak stay virgins, the strong win women (Comikey blurb); the hero announces his goal openly (MyAnimeList reviews).
delivery.note: The premise announces its values openly as comedy; no counter-view is noted in sources, apart from the heroines' resistance and the hero's insistence on consent.

personified.ideology: Strength and effort earn the partners you want

116809.dominant: Hedonism, Strength rules, Expressive individualism, Pragmatism.

42888.heading: Happy Marriage?!
42888.label: From summaries
42888.life_message: A marriage that starts as a bargain can become real love if both partners keep choosing each other, learn to talk and stand together against the past.

content.framing: Mixed: attacks on Chiwa condemned; the husband's hitting not clearly judged (to verify)

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Endorsed within marriage; some coercive behavior played as romance

delivery.evidence: The message comes through the couple's fights and reconciliations; the plotting relatives are drawn as villains, while the husband's flaws are treated as part of his charm (ANN; TV Tropes).
delivery.note: A formula romance in which the stated goal (a happy marriage) is never in doubt; the drama lies in misunderstandings and family secrets.

personified.ideology: Devotion, duty and a wish to be heard

42888.dominant: Traditionalism (marriage and the family line), Confucian ethics (filial duty and the household), with a romance of possessive devotion.

86655.heading: Happy Sugar Life
86655.label: From summaries
86655.life_message: Love that hides, owns and kills to keep another person is not love but a cage; the series traces abuse passing from adults to children and ends with its "sweet life" built on murder and death.

content.framing: Shown from the killer's sympathetic view; ends in death and arrests
Condemned (abuse shown as harm), but the teen-child bond is framed as romance

delivery.evidence: No character states a moral; healthy love is voiced by Shouko and Asahi, who are killed or rejected; abusers are drawn as extreme caricatures (This Week in Anime).
delivery.note: Told largely from Satou's point of view, with sweet imagery (candy, moon, angels) over horror; the verdict comes only through the ending.

86655.dominant: Nihilism (Explored), Expressive individualism (Critiqued: love as a private law), Hedonism (Critiqued).

98204.heading: Haru's Curse
98204.label: From summaries
98204.life_message: Grief and guilt cannot be outrun by living inside a dead loved one's memory; the living honor the dead by being honest about their own love and by choosing their own lives.

content.framing: Endorsed (adult romance); hinted sister attachment left ambiguous

delivery.evidence: No lectures: the message comes through the seasonal chapters, Haru's own diary and her late-chapter point of view, which complicate every character's assumptions (TheOASG; Renote). Togo's mother's view is shown as rigid, not villainous.
delivery.note: Reviewers stress that the romance is secondary to the characters' recovery (But Why Tho?).

personified.ideology: Grief and guilt, moving toward self-determination
Family duty, moving toward his own choice

98204.dominant: Existentialism (making one's life one's own), Expressive individualism, Traditionalism (critiqued: arranged marriage and family authority).

78649.heading: Haven't You Heard? I'm Sakamoto
78649.label: From summaries
78649.life_message: Meeting hostility with composure, kindness and style can change the people around you; the coolest thing is to help others and refuse revenge.

delivery.evidence: A gag comedy in which Sakamoto's example, not speeches, wins people over; he does give one speech about believing in friends at graduation (ch. 24).
delivery.note: Antagonists are mocked but also redeemed and shielded, so the opposing view (envy, revenge) is shown failing rather than argued down.

personified.ideology: manipulating others to tear down the admired

78649.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (kindness, magnanimity), Stoicism (composure), Absurdism (surreal comedy).

30696.heading: Hayate the Combat Butler
30696.label: From summaries
30696.life_message: Honest work and loyalty can lift you out of the worst start, and growing up means standing on your own feet and letting the people you love be free.

content.framing: Mixed: harem comedy and light fan service played for laughs; romance chaste

delivery.evidence: The parents are faceless shadows with "Mother" and "Father" written on them (Wikipedia, characters); morals arrive through gags and Nagi's choices, not speeches; Hata prioritized gags over plot at times (Reverse Thieves, citing ch. 387).
delivery.note: A gag comedy whose serious message (work, loyalty, growing up) builds slowly and lands in the final arc.

30696.dominant: Expressive individualism (Nagi's self-reliance), Consumerism (wealth satirized and given up), Classical virtue ethics (work and loyalty), Communitarianism (the Violet Mansion household).

111101.heading: Hazure Skill: The Guild Member with a Worthless Skill Is Actually a Legendary Assassin
111101.label: From summaries
111101.life_message: Ordinary work and quiet service can be worth more than glory, and even a trained killer can choose a normal life; the story also rewards its hero's power with the devotion of many women.

content.framing: Endorsed as the hero's skill; villains punished
Endorsed (casual sex as reward and comedy)

111101.dominant: Hedonism, Might makes right (explored), Pragmatism, Expressive individualism.

delivery.evidence: The "ordinary life" wish is stated in the premise; the sexual rewards and the hero's power are presented without question (Anime UK News; MangaUpdates).
delivery.note: There is little argument in the story; it is a wish-fulfillment fantasy whose values are carried by what the hero gets.

personified.ideology: Hidden power, quiet work, pleasure without cost
Preying on the weak for profit

108832.heading: HEART GEAR
108832.label: From summaries
108832.life_message: What makes someone a person is the heart they choose, not the body or program they were given; a family can be made by anyone who chooses to care, and a world ruined by war can still be given a second chance.

content.framing: Mixed: protective fighting endorsed; domination and war condemned

delivery.evidence: Hild's case for killing Roue is given its reasons before Chrome refuses (ciatr); D and R argue opposite plans for humanity (VIZ vol. 7).
delivery.note: The message comes through action and through the family's choices; the final volume becomes more talk-driven as Roue hears D and R (Manga News).

personified.ideology: Choose your own purpose; protect those you love
Order through total control of others' wills
Security through sacrificing one for many
Welcome versus eliminate the last human

108832.dominant: Existentialism (Chrome chooses his own purpose), Communitarianism (made family), Transhumanism (machine minds and souls), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued in Wodan).

101942.heading: Heavenly Delusion
101942.label: From summaries
101942.life_message: People are more than the bodies and labels others give them; "heaven" built by people who control and lie is a hell, and the only heaven worth finding is the small place you make with someone who sees who you really are.

content.framing: Mixed: assault condemned; teen intimacy shown tenderly and unjudged

delivery.evidence: Takahara's rulers are given reasons (a cure, a new order), and Dr. Sawatari's transplant is explained as an attempt to save one life (fan wiki); Robin and the cult are drawn as plainly evil; Ishiguro withholds answers to keep the mystery.
delivery.note: The series rarely states a message; it shows consequences and leaves readers to judge, consistent with Ishiguro's stated aim to make readers feel fear and caution (Wikipedia).

personified.ideology: Love and loyalty that look past bodies and labels
Identity chosen and lived across a body that is not one's own
Remake humanity under a planned order
Science to save life, at a cost

101942.dominant: Transhumanism (critiqued), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Existentialism and Progressivism (gender identity, explored).

86720.heading: Helck
86720.label: From summaries
86720.life_message: Hatred taught by rulers can be undone by seeing the other side for yourself; even after terrible betrayal, choosing to save your enemies instead of destroying them, and letting friends share your burden, opens a hopeful future.

delivery.evidence: The truth about the demons is revealed through Helck's past (ch. 36-52); ANN's anime reviewer felt the classism theme was 'beaten over our heads,' but the Human King is given a tragic motive (saving the Ancients).
delivery.note: The anti-prejudice message is carried by a long flashback and by the heroes' choice to save the humans; it is stated directly at times, but villains are given reasons.

personified.ideology: Protective strength and mercy toward former enemies
Loyal skepticism; trust earned by evidence
Rule by command; any cost to save his cause
A new world by any means

129882.heading: Hell Mode: The Hardcore Gamer Dominates Another World with Garbage Balancing - Summoner of the Beginning
129882.label: From summaries
129882.life_message: Steady, patient effort and love for one's family can lift a person out of a low station, and strength earned the hard way is meant to protect others.

content.framing: Neutral (monster hunting as progress); human villainy condemned

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: The value of grinding is stated constantly through Allen's gamer logic (fan wiki); villains are greedy nobles drawn simply (Japanese Wikipedia); ANN calls the manga more stereotypical than the books.
delivery.note: The message about effort is built into the premise and narration rather than argued.

129882.dominant: Pragmatism, Communitarianism, Might makes right (explored as a talent-and-level order).

109661.heading: Hello, Melancholic!
109661.label: From summaries
109661.life_message: Someone who was hurt for standing out can find her voice again through friends who want her as she is, and real friendship sometimes means a push past your fears.

content.framing: Endorsed (same-sex teen romance as the heart of the story)

delivery.evidence: The story carries its message through the band's practice and concert; no character argues against same-sex romance or for exclusion, and the bullies are not given a voice (Drunken Anime Blog; Okazu).
delivery.note: Healing and romance are shown, not preached; the setting has no social pushback to argue with.

personified.ideology: Fear of standing out after rejection

109661.dominant: Expressive individualism, Communitarianism (found family of the band), Progressivism (affirmed same-sex romance).

100994.heading: Hell's Paradise: Jigokuraku (Yuji Kaku, 2018-2021)
100994.label: From summaries
100994.life_message: A good life is an ordinary, chosen one: love that gives you a reason to live, honest bonds formed across enemy lines, and balance instead of extremes. Immortality bought by harvesting others, and obedience that empties out the self, are what the story rejects.

content.framing: Mixed: brutality shown as horrible; also staged as spectacular action

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: married love honored; ritual sex shown as part of the villains' power; nudity frequent

delivery.evidence: Kaku built the Tensen as the opposites of the criminals and executioners (ANN, 2025); the message comes through Gabimaru's love and Sagiri's inner struggle rather than lectures.
delivery.note: Theme statements about yin-yang and balance are made inside battle explanations; villains (the Tensen) are given backstories but stay monstrous.

personified.ideology: Love and an ordinary life over killing
Duty with mercy; balance of strength and weakness

100994.dominant: Existentialism (affirmed: love as chosen meaning), Buddhist ideas (the Middle Way, explored), Pantheist/New Age (Taoist life-energy and yin-yang, explored), Transhumanism (immortality, critiqued), Bushido / honor code (the executioners' code, explored).

30267.heading: Hellsing
30267.label: From summaries
30267.life_message: Being human is a choice of will: those who stay human and fight to the end are worthy of respect, while those who trade their humanity for power, immortality or a faith turned to hatred become monsters.

content.framing: Stylized and celebrated as spectacle; villains' cruelty also shown
Sexual violence shown as trauma and condemned; fan service unjudged

delivery.evidence: Characters state the themes in long speeches (Alucard on humans and monsters, the Major on war, Anderson and Maxwell on faith); each side argues its case, but the Major and Maxwell are drawn as grotesques.
delivery.note: Ideas are delivered by speeches between battles; Hirano's author notes mock the series' seriousness (Thompson).

personified.ideology: Only a human can defeat a monster; he gave up his humanity
War for its own sake; human by will alone
Faith as holy war on monsters and heretics

30267.dominant: Existentialism (humanity as a choice), Christian (explored through sectarian war and Vlad's fall), Might makes right (explored), Patriotism / nationalism (Integra's Crown against a Nazi remnant).

33104.heading: Helter Skelter: Fashion Unfriendly
33104.label: From summaries
33104.life_message: A life built on manufactured beauty and the public's gaze consumes itself and the people around it; the story offers this as a warning, and it spreads the blame to the industry and the audience, not only to Liliko.

delivery.evidence: The critique is carried by events, not lectures; Silverman (ANN) says the book implicates its readers; the investigator states the warning to Liliko directly (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: A cautionary tale with an ambiguous epilogue; the story avoids simple retribution (The Slings and Arrows).

33104.dominant: Consumerism critiqued (the beauty and celebrity industries), Feminism (beauty standards on women), Hedonism critiqued, Expressive individualism critiqued.

123261.heading: Her Majesty's Swarm
123261.label: From summaries
123261.life_message: Victory sought for its own sake devours the one who seeks it: a queen who answers cruelty with greater cruelty loses her own humanity, and the war leaves only ruin. (The story's own verdict is debated by readers.)

content.framing: Mixed: the queen's slaughter is shown without restraint; the story's verdict is debated
Condemned (perpetrators are slavers and enemies), to verify

delivery.evidence: The story shows the queen's point of view without comment; enemies are often caricatures (slavers, zealots), though the point of view sometimes shifts to the humans (Goodreads). Readers disagree on whether it endorses or critiques her.
delivery.note: No message is stated; the moral weight depends on how the reader takes the queen's fall.

personified.character: The church of the God of Light

123261.dominant: Might makes right (explored: conquest for victory's sake); Collectivism/authoritarianism (the hive mind swallowing the self); Nihilism (victory with no meaning); Christian (a fictional church of the God of Light shown as zealous; angels and a devil figure).

105279.heading: Hero Without a Class: Who Even Needs Skills?!
105279.label: From summaries
105279.life_message: Hard work, learning from others and a loving family carry you further than the gifts you were handed at birth, even when everyone says you have none.

delivery.evidence: Arel argues that hard work can pay off (Anime UK News); those who doubt him are simply proven wrong, and Anime Feminist finds the tone condescending.
delivery.note: The effort message is voiced through Arel's own reasoning and confirmed by every win; the opposing view (class decides worth) is never given a real defender.

personified.ideology: Effort and learning beat inborn gifts

105279.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Pragmatism, Stoicism, Communitarianism.

74501.heading: Hi Score Girl
74501.label: From summaries
