delivery.evidence: No character states a moral; villains are given abuse and trauma backstories (Yoshie, Minami, Mitsuru); Oshikiri framed it as fear created by ordinary people (Japanese Wikipedia, citing the vol. 3 afterword).
delivery.note: The story shows cause and consequence and lets the ending speak; readers draw opposite lessons (catharsis versus warning).

75721.dominant: Nihilism (a world without rescue, explored), Might makes right (bullying hierarchy and revenge, critiqued), Communitarianism (the closed village, critiqued).

98388.heading: Living-Room Matsunaga-san
98388.label: From summaries
98388.life_message: A house of strangers can become a family, and real love is patient: it looks after the other person, sets limits for their good, and lets a young person grow up first.

content.framing: Mixed: the romance is framed as sweet and true; the adult sets a boundary of waiting until she graduates
Neutral; one drunk scene shown as unfair to Meeko

delivery.evidence: No speeches reported; the message comes through household life and Matsunaga's decision to wait (vols. 8-9). The creator says she wanted readers to come away thinking share houses are nice (Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: A slow romance carried by daily life rather than a stated thesis; rival suitors (Ryo, the ex) are treated with sympathy, not as strawmen.

personified.ideology: Earnest first love and growing up
Pleasure and casual romance, later settling down

98388.dominant: Communitarianism (found family in a share house), Classical virtue ethics (patience and restraint), Duty ethics (waiting until graduation).

30904.heading: Lone Wolf and Cub
30904.label: From summaries
30904.life_message: A father who refuses a corrupt order walks the road of vengeance with his son, and the bond between them is the one pure thing on that road; revenge costs everything, and only an act of love at the very end breaks the cycle of hatred.

content.framing: Mixed: killings shown as skilled and often honorable; their cost to Daigorō and the innocent is shown
Mixed: sexual violence shown as villainy; nudity and eroticism frequent and unjudged
Mixed: shown as the road to hell, but the hero is admired

delivery.evidence: Many stories center on a philosophical point or an aspect of feudal life (skjam); opponents such as Shino Sakon argue against Ittō and are given full dignity (PopMatters); Retsudō gets the final act of grace.
delivery.note: The message is carried by episodes and silences rather than speeches; Koike said a strong character lets the story develop on its own (Wikipedia).

personified.ideology: Fidelity to a chosen road of vengeance; fatherhood
Laying down the sword; humane equality

30904.dominant: Bushido / honor code (rejected and embodied), Stoicism, Buddhist ideas (meifumadō), Traditionalism.

107540.heading: Loner Life in Another World
107540.label: From summaries
107540.life_message: You do not need the best gifts or a crowd to do good: someone who uses what he has with wit can protect the people around him, and may find he was never as alone as he thought.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: fan service played as comedy; coercion by villains condemned

delivery.evidence: Haruka narrates almost everything and lectures Tanaka on the difference between stealing power and growing (Wikipedia, anime ep. 6); ANN reviewers find the monologue tiresome. The Delinquents are flat villains; Tanaka gets a motive (a loner like Haruka) but no sympathy.
delivery.note: The message about using what you have is carried by action and by Haruka's constant commentary.

personified.ideology: Self-reliance and ingenuity that end in caring for others
A resentful loner who takes from others

107540.dominant: Pragmatism, Communitarianism (found family), Might makes right (critiqued), Expressive individualism.

136807.heading: Look Back
136807.label: From summaries
136807.life_message: A good life is spent making things with and for other people. Talent and rivalry are not enough; art is worth the grind because of who it is shared with. Loss cannot be undone, but it can be carried forward into work.

delivery.evidence: Polygon praised its subtlety (via Wikipedia); ANN notes how much it conveys with little dialogue; no reviewer found calls it preachy.
delivery.note: The message is carried by images and silence; Fujino's despair gets a full hearing before the last pages answer it with a memory, not a speech.

personified.ideology: Art as ambition, then art for another
Art as devotion and a way out of isolation

136807.dominant: Existentialism (choosing to go on), Secular humanism (meaning in people and work), Classical virtue ethics (diligence and craft), Stoicism (accepting loss).

111390.heading: Love After World Domination
111390.label: From summaries
111390.life_message: Love can cross the lines that groups draw, and people are more than the side they were assigned.

content.framing: Romance endorsed; fan service as comedy

delivery.evidence: Both sides are drawn sympathetically (Bosslar's courtesy, the princesses' friendships); the message is carried by the couple's story rather than speeches (ANN vol. 1; Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The idea that labels like hero and villain are not the whole person is shown through comedy, not argued.

111390.dominant: Expressive individualism (love chosen over the side you were assigned); romantic comedy; Super Sentai parody.

61185.heading: Love at Fourteen
61185.label: From summaries
61185.life_message: First love at fourteen is real and worth taking seriously; growing up means dropping the act and being honest about what you feel, even when time together is short.

content.framing: Mixed: the young couple's feelings treated with tenderness; the teacher's interest in a student presented gently and not clearly condemned (to verify)

delivery.evidence: Interior monologues and quiet moments carry the feelings (Kate Dacey; WWAC); short puberty "definitions" between chapters are informational, not moral (Suitable for Treatment).
delivery.note: The series presents feelings and moods rather than arguments; it does not comment on the age gaps in its side stories, leaving readers to judge.

personified.ideology: An adult's care blurred with romantic feeling

61185.dominant: Expressive individualism (dropping the mask), Communitarianism (the class as a small world), Confucian ethics (role expectations), Existentialism.

171729.heading: Love Bullet
171729.label: From summaries
171729.life_message: Love means wanting the other person's happiness, even when it is not with you; grief can be honored and still let go of.

content.framing: Neutral (stylized action-comedy); reckless shooting criticized through Chiyo

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe the message as carried by Koharu's choices and the grief story (ANN; The A.V. Club); Chiyo's fight-first attitude is shown as a rival view that softens rather than a strawman.
delivery.note: Love as wanting another's happiness emerges through action-comedy missions and a bittersweet backstory; no character lectures.

personified.ideology: self-giving love; care for each match
fighting for the thrill; might settles disputes

171729.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (self-giving love and courage), Expressive individualism, Progressivism (matches regardless of gender).

30031.heading: Love★Com
30031.label: From summaries
30031.life_message: Love grows out of honest friendship and the courage to say what you feel, and the right person may not match what others expect.

content.framing: Mixed: chaste teen romance endorsed; forced kisses and the threat condemned

delivery.evidence: Carried by the comedy and the romance; ANN praises the quiet, understated confession in vol. 7; the grandfather and Hitomi are flat antagonists, while rivals like Mimi and Kohori are given sympathy.
delivery.note: The idea that a couple need not fit outside expectations is never lectured; it comes through two people who keep choosing each other.

personified.ideology: Family control over a grandchild's partner

30031.dominant: Expressive individualism, Communitarianism, Classical virtue ethics (friendship into romance; courage and constancy).

30016.heading: Love Hina
30016.label: From summaries
30016.life_message: Keep trying after failure and keep faith with the people and promises you love; stubborn, kindly persistence wins both the goal and the girl.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy; consent ignored in gags; ends in marriage

delivery.evidence: Reviewers treat it as a comedy with no message pressed (ANN, Chen: a laugh-out-loud joyride; Manga Bookshelf); perseverance is shown through Keitaro's repeated tries, not argued.
delivery.note: Perseverance and promise-keeping come through the plot; the comedy never questions its own fan service or slapstick.

personified.ideology: Discipline of the sword; suspicion of men

30016.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (perseverance), Traditionalism (promise and marriage), Hedonism (comedy of pleasure), Bushido / honor code (Motoko, as comedy).

85566.heading: Love & Lies
85566.label: From summaries
85566.life_message: Love has to be chosen freely and honestly; no system can assign the heart, though choosing someone means hurting someone else.

content.framing: Mixed: young love endorsed; sexual tension and fan service played straight

delivery.evidence: The law's benefits are stated (stable birth rate, per the fan wiki) and its officials are drawn as people, not monsters; the story's sympathy stays with the teens' feelings rather than arguing the policy.
delivery.note: The message is carried by the triangle's emotions and every chapter title's pairing of love and lies, not by speeches about policy.

personified.ideology: The heart over the assigned match
Planned marriage for the common good
Love the system never accounted for

85566.dominant: Expressive individualism (the heart over the notice), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Utilitarianism (explored).

104140.heading: Love Me for Who I Am
104140.label: From summaries
104140.life_message: Everyone deserves to be seen and loved as who they really are, and a circle of friends who accept you can help you heal and even help your family learn to accept you.

delivery.evidence: Characters correct misgendering and explain identity directly; Anime Feminist notes that transphobic moments are usually followed by a lesson; ANN found close-minded views given more space than Mogumo's own inner life.
delivery.note: The message is spoken outright in teachable moments, but the father and Kotone are given reasons and arcs rather than drawn as pure villains.

personified.ideology: Non-binary identity; be seen as you are
Hiding oneself by controlling a friend

104140.dominant: Progressivism (gender inclusion), Expressive individualism, Communitarianism (found family).

86219.heading: Love Me, Love Me Not
86219.label: From summaries
86219.life_message: Love grows when you are honest with yourself and considerate of others: a shy dreamer finds courage, a guarded realist learns to trust, and real friendship survives rejection, jealousy and family pressure.

delivery.evidence: Yuna's fate-based and Akari's practical views of love are both given a voice and both revised (The Graphic Library; Wikipedia).
delivery.note: Lessons come through inner monologue and conversations between friends, not lectures.

86219.dominant: Expressive individualism (honesty with one's own feelings), Communitarianism (friendship), Pragmatism (realism about love).

99435.heading: Love of Kill
99435.label: From summaries
99435.life_message: People shaped by violence can still choose who they are: the name you take, the family that raised you and the partner you trust as an equal matter more than blood, rank or the past.

content.framing: Neutral (professional killing as action); trafficking and war-making condemned
Mixed: an adult romance with sexual tension; nothing explicit reported
Endorsed as romance, with some critical distance

delivery.evidence: The chosen-family theme is shown through events (Chateau declaring herself a Dankworth); villains like Donny get backstory but little sympathy; Hou and Nikka are given motives (Wikipedia episode summaries).
delivery.note: No lessons are stated; the story lets the romance and the reveal of the past carry its view of names, guilt and family.

personified.ideology: Possessive, protective love; living under a borrowed name
Orphans as weapons; war for profit
Revenge and loyalty to a mentor

99435.dominant: Might makes right, Existentialism (identity and names), Communitarianism (chosen family).

107445.heading: Love’s in Sight!
107445.label: From summaries
107445.life_message: People are more than their labels, blind or delinquent: love and friendship grow when each person sees the other whole, and a fair world makes room for everyone to live an ordinary life.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: ANN guide (Lemus) says it toes the line on being didactic; Honey's Anime calls it educational but in good taste; the disability scholars praise how it teaches techniques through humor (Review of Disability Studies).
delivery.note: Lessons about accessibility arrive as gags and small scenes; prejudiced views are carried by minor figures who are corrected, and the overprotective sister is shown with compassion rather than as a villain.

personified.ideology: Looking past labels; learning to help properly
Protective love that limits a disabled sibling
Hiding who one is for fear of rejection
The street belongs to the sighted

55081.heading: Love Stage!!
55081.label: From summaries
55081.life_message: Love is for a person, not a gender or a part to play: Ryoma loves Izumi once he knows who he really is, and Izumi finds the courage to follow his own dream in a family that wanted another one for him.

content.framing: Mixed: the adult same-sex romance and sex are endorsed; Ryoma's early assault is regretted but forgiven and partly played as comedy; assaults by strangers condemned
Mixed: often played as romance or comedy, sometimes corrected

delivery.evidence: Ryoma's change of heart is shown through his anger, denial and decision (Kotaku); vol. 7 has the couple reflect on what it means for a man to love a man (SuBLime); the family's casual response to the early assault goes unchallenged (Fandom.com).
delivery.note: The romance and its message are delivered through comedy and melodrama, with no lectures; the series rarely steps back to judge its own coercive scenes.

personified.ideology: Follow your own calling; be loved for who you are
Love transcends gender; devotion that must learn respect

136943.heading: Love, That's an Understatement
136943.label: From summaries
136943.life_message: Strength includes letting others help you; people are more than their reputations, and love grows when two people learn to rely on each other.

content.framing: Protective fighting admired; gang violence shown as a danger
Endorsed as sweet first love; one surprise kiss questioned by ANN

delivery.evidence: Risa's change is carried by events (repeated rescues, a sick visit, a night at Zen's home); ANN notes she partly recognizes her own need to seem perfect. Rivals are given sympathetic sides (Fuumin's hard work, vol. 7).
delivery.note: The message about accepting help is clear but not lectured in sources opened.

personified.ideology: Rival who channels drive into study

136943.dominant: Interdependence over self-reliance; looking past reputations; protective first love.

101255.heading: Lovesick Ellie
101255.label: From summaries
101255.life_message: Being loved for who you really are, odd, plain and openly longing, is better than any polished image; when two people drop their masks with each other, love can last.

content.framing: Mixed: sexual daydreaming played as comedy; a committed teen couple; first sex implied, not shown
Mixed: played for laughs, then shown to have costs

delivery.evidence: The authenticity theme is shown through the couple's secrets; the father's objection is treated with sympathy rather than mocked (ciatr; Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: A comedy where the message (be known for who you are) is acted out, not argued.

personified.ideology: Honest desire; the true self over the image

101255.dominant: Expressive individualism (authenticity over image), Classical virtue ethics (honesty), Communitarianism (friends and family).

40552.heading: Lucifer and the Biscuit Hammer
40552.label: From summaries
40552.life_message: Even a person taught to trust no one can find reasons to live through friends, mentors and love; caring for the world, rather than owning or ending it, is what makes a life worth having.

content.framing: Lechery played as comedy and punished with slapstick; romance sincere

delivery.evidence: Creamer (ANN, v9-10) says the themes of family, childhood and adulthood and regained faith in the world come through the final fight as a declaration of love; TWIA finds Yuuhi's early nihilism heavy-handed but his arc earned.
delivery.note: Yuuhi's movement from contempt for the world to finding reasons to live is carried by his bonds with Samidare and the other knights, not by speeches.

personified.ideology: Misanthropy turning to meaning through bonds
Wish to own the world by destroying it
Protective adulthood that must learn to trust

40552.dominant: Existentialism (meaning chosen through bonds), Nihilism (critiqued), Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism.

30705.heading: Lunar Legend Tsukihime
30705.label: From summaries
30705.life_message: Even someone who carries death in his eyes can choose to protect life, and love can reach across the gulf between human and monster; facing the truth of one's past is the way through.

content.framing: Neutral (horror action); the killer impulse condemned
Romance endorsed; the attempted rape condemned

delivery.evidence: The message is carried by Shiki's choices and the romance; villains like Roa are given power and menace (Tropedia), and SHIKI is made tragic rather than evil (Tropedia).
delivery.note: A horror romance with little moralizing; the closest thing to a stated view is Shiki's calm about death, "just living is enough" (Type-Moon wiki, game characterization).

personified.ideology: Innocent love restraining a predator's nature
Immortality and power at any cost

30705.dominant: Pagan/occult (vampires, magecraft, demon bloodlines) and Existentialism (living with the sight of death), with the Church as a hard, sympathetic presence.

35709.heading: Lychee Light Club
35709.label: From summaries
35709.life_message: A group that worships beauty, youth and its leader's will destroys itself, and the machine it built to serve that will learns what its makers never did: that being human means not killing.

content.framing: Shown with consequences (the club destroys itself), but aestheticized
Condemned in outcome; aestheticized in art (ero-guro)

delivery.evidence: TCJ calls the book largely amoral but faults a heavy-handed moral ending; Manga Bookshelf argues the moralizing may be the point, with Lychee taught that wrong is wrong.
delivery.note: The fascist ideal is satirized through its own adherents' grotesque theatricality; the moral turns explicit at the end through Kanon and Lychee.

personified.ideology: Fascist dictatorship and the cult of youth and beauty
A machine learning humanity, art and mercy
Christian mercy; being human means not killing

35709.dominant: Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Might makes right (critiqued), Nihilism (explored), Pacifism / nonviolence (Lychee's lesson, affirmed).

98285.heading: Machimaho: I Messed Up and Made the Wrong Person Into a Magical Girl!
98285.label: From summaries
98285.life_message: On the surface the joke is that raw force and attitude win; underneath, the story slowly reveals a neglected girl who will fight anyone except the few people she cares about, and asks what made her that way.

content.framing: Played for comedy; Kayo's brutality is the central joke
Fan service played for laughs; not judged
Shown, briefly undercut early; explored later

delivery.evidence: Souryu says the plot follows Kayo's personality and logic rather than a planned message (ddnavi); reviewers find no lecture, only parody.
delivery.note: The parody is the point; the later family and friendship arcs carry what values there are.

98285.dominant: Absurdism (genre parody), Strength rules, Expressive individualism, Nihilism (light).

57989.heading: Maga-tsuki
57989.label: From summaries
57989.life_message: Kindness that treats the lonely, even an unwanted goddess of misfortune, as an equal turns calamity into happiness; the story rewards that kindness with a shared household and a shrine carried on to the next generation.

content.framing: Played for comedy (harem fan service endorsed); ends in plural marriage

delivery.evidence: AIPT and Anime UK News describe a formulaic harem comedy with almost no plot (vol. 1); Neo calls it harmless fun (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: No argued viewpoint; the values (kindness, family duty, the harem as reward) are carried by the comedy and the ending.

57989.dominant: Pagan/occult (Shinto kami and shrine life), Communitarianism, Traditionalism, Hedonism.

78025.heading: Magi: The Adventures of Sinbad
78025.label: From summaries
78025.life_message: A leader who believes a country must never throw away its people can build a better world through courage, trade and loyal friends, but power and ambition carry a heavy price.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; war condemned, heroic combat celebrated
Mixed: humiliation played as comedy; coerced marriage condemned

delivery.evidence: Badr's speech to the villagers about what war did to his body and Sinbad's line that a country that abandons its citizens should not exist state the theme openly (fan wiki); ANN calls the futility of war a central motif. Villains such as Barbarossa and Umm Madaura are drawn without much depth, while Drakon and Serendine argue for duty and are given full dignity.
delivery.note: The message is stated in a few key speeches and otherwise carried by adventure and statecraft; Sinbad's ambition is left deliberately ambiguous, foreshadowing the main series.

personified.ideology: Ambition joined to care for others
Military duty and a soldier's pride

78025.dominant: Patriotism / nationalism (founding a nation that protects its people), Pragmatism (trade over war), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued in Parthevia), Communitarianism (the gathered companions).

30119.heading: Magic Knight Rayearth
30119.label: From summaries
30119.life_message: Friendship and a heart that refuses to give up can carry ordinary girls through great trials, but a heroic quest can hide hard truths: when love and duty collide, doing what must be done can still break your heart.

content.framing: Neutral (fantasy battles); the deaths at the end framed as tragic

delivery.evidence: The Manga Critic quotes dialogue on the heart controlling everything and calls the script painfully earnest; Graphic Novel Reporter says it beats the reader over the head with "friends forever." The ending complicates the simple quest.
delivery.note: Friendship and willpower are stated outright; the darker message about duty and love arrives in the twist at the end.

personified.ideology: A strong heart and loyalty to friends
Wise authority that hides the truth

30119.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (courage, loyalty), Duty ethics (duty against love), Communitarianism (sisterhood).

110022.heading: Magic Stone Gourmet: Eating Magical Power Made Me The Strongest
110022.label: From summaries
110022.life_message: A child dismissed for a "useless" gift finds his worth among people who love him, and grows by effort and responsibility into a prince able to protect his family and his kingdom.

delivery.evidence: The skill-ranking father and stepmother exist mainly to be left behind (Mangapedia; MyAnimeList synopsis); the message that worth is not a skill score is carried by plot rather than speeches. Lloyd's lesson that effort matters is stated (Mangapedia).
delivery.note: A light power fantasy whose values (family, effort, duty) are built into the premise.

personified.ideology: Loyal, hard-working heir; worth beyond one's skill

110022.dominant: Traditionalism (family and crown), Communitarianism (the royal family as refuge), Patriotism / nationalism (loyalty to Ishtarica against Heim).

70175.heading: Magical Girl Apocalypse
70175.label: From summaries
70175.life_message: Wishing for excitement to escape a dull life can bring horror; what finally saves the world is love and the willingness to give your life for others.

content.framing: Mixed: sexual threats condemned in the moment; harassment by a main ally played as comedy

delivery.evidence: Horror spectacle drives the story (AniList Gore, Zombie, Survival); Kii's change from passivity is shown through choices; the villain's godhood plan is drawn as pure evil.
delivery.note: Any message about boredom, courage and sacrifice sits under survival horror and is not argued out.

personified.ideology: Love and a hidden cruel self

70175.dominant: Nihilism (explored), Might makes right (critiqued), Pagan/occult (demon pact as plot), Transhumanism (engineered magical girls and fusions).

85666.heading: Magical Girl Site
85666.label: From summaries
85666.life_message: Even the most crushed person can choose to protect others instead of passing on their pain; misfortune does not have to make you cruel, and happiness is worth fighting for.

content.framing: Mixed: abuse and murder condemned; some revenge killings shown with sympathy
Mixed: assaults condemned; fan service of young girls not condemned
Shown with consequences; self-harm also used as a power

delivery.evidence: The King's and Kaname's contempt for humanity are given space but are defeated by Aya's refusal to give up; ANN finds the cruelty over-the-top rather than argued.
delivery.note: The message comes through events and Aya's choices rather than speeches, inside a story most reviewers describe as shock-driven.

personified.ideology: Kindness and choosing to live despite misery
Misanthropy and the wish to be a god
Humanity judged by its "negative energy" and culled
Cruelty that can turn to loyalty

85666.dominant: Nihilism (critiqued: the King's and Kaname's contempt for humanity), Might makes right (critiqued), Communitarianism (the girls' alliance), with a questioned Utilitarianism behind the Tempest.

87056.heading: Magical Sempai
87056.label: From summaries
87056.life_message: Keep practicing what you love even when you fail in front of people; a patient friend who sees you at your worst is worth more than a perfect show.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy (fan service is the main draw)

delivery.evidence: There is little explicit message; Madara's skeptical, modest view gets a fair, recurring voice as a foil.
delivery.note: A gag strip: each mini-chapter is a trick, a failure and a punchline.

personified.ideology: Science and modesty; magic is fraud

87056.dominant: Hedonism (pleasure in teasing and display), Communitarianism (a club of friends), Naturalism (magic explained as skill and science).

85230.heading: Magika Swordsman and Summoner
85230.label: From summaries
85230.life_message: Strength comes from the bonds you form with others; a young man who honors the family that raised him, refuses to abandon his friends and earns trust can rise from the lowest rank to lead his country.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy and as the power system

delivery.evidence: The rule that power comes from bonds is stated by Leme (ch. 4-5) and repeated each arc; opponents include fair rivals (Kanae, Beatrix) and cardboard villains (the headmaster's conspiracy).
delivery.note: The message about bonds is stated outright, while the fan service is never commented on.

85230.dominant: Communitarianism ("power of bonds"), Hedonism (harem as reward), Bushido / honor code (the Hayashizaki sword way), Patriotism / nationalism (the king who defends Japan).

140482.heading: Magilumiere Magical Girls Inc.
140482.label: From summaries
140482.life_message: Careful, honest work done together, and refusing to treat people as expendable for profit, is how ordinary people protect one another and find their place.

content.framing: Neutral (monster-extermination action); human cruelty and experimentation condemned

delivery.evidence: The safety-versus-profit argument is carried by plot (spells built from field data, mutations caused by large-scale magic); Koga's results-first view gets a sympathetic backstory and is partly vindicated, while Kamakura and Tsutsumi are drawn as plain schemers (fan wiki; Japanese Wikipedia; ANN).
delivery.note: Reviewers call the corporate critique pointed (ANN) and sharp (Anime Feminist) but none call it preachy; ANN's season 2 critics compare its boardroom scenes to Succession.

personified.ideology: Worker safety and efficient magic over profit
Revenge for being used as a test subject

140482.dominant: Pragmatism, Communitarianism, Critical theory (critique of corporate power and deregulation), Duty ethics.

101131.heading: Magus of the Library
101131.label: From summaries
101131.life_message: Knowledge and stories belong to everyone, a person's worth does not depend on birth, race or poverty, and because words can heal or destroy, the truth in books must be protected and handled with care.

delivery.evidence: Narration states the value of texts directly (ch. 1; fan wiki), but the book-ban inquiry gives both sides (v7) and the terrorist leader explains his vision at length (v7-8).
delivery.note: The message is carried by Theo's rise and by debates inside the Library rather than by a single speech; some chapters are lecture-like.

personified.ideology: Become the protagonist of your own story
Prejudice against the poor and different, later unlearned
Equality by force; no room for the weak

101131.dominant: Liberalism (free access to books and the censorship debate), Classical virtue ethics, Secular humanism, Progressivism (anti-racism).

30688.heading: Maison Ikkoku
30688.label: From summaries
30688.life_message: Lasting love is patient and faithful: loving again does not betray the dead, and a hapless young man becomes worthy of marriage by growing up, finding his work and keeping faith.

content.framing: Mixed: voyeurism and harassment played as comedy; the leads' one night framed as loving and leading to marriage

delivery.evidence: Takahashi set out to write a love story that could happen in the real world (Wikipedia); the rivals are treated with sympathy and given happy endings.
delivery.note: The message comes through slow character growth and comedy, not speeches; the clearest statement is Godai's declaration (ch. 151) and Kyoko's one condition (ch. 158).

personified.ideology: Patient, faithful love; growing into responsibility
Grief and fidelity to the dead

30688.dominant: Traditionalism (marriage and family blessing), Communitarianism (the boarding house as found family), Classical virtue ethics (patience and fidelity).

143516.heading: Make the Exorcist Fall in Love
143516.label: From summaries
143516.life_message: Faith that is beaten into a child and obeyed out of fear is not love; a person must be free to heal, to feel and to choose their own path, and love freely given can redeem even someone sent to deceive.

content.framing: Mixed: sexual violence condemned; consensual desire treated as normal and healthy
Shown as harm, not a model

delivery.evidence: Characters state the thesis (Dante's advice, ch. 1; the boy's speech to Lucifer, ch. 97), but churchmen like Daniel and Heisenberg are given reasons, demons are given backstories, and the boy's faith is never mocked.
delivery.note: The message is carried by the boy's healing arc and stated outright at turning points; the Church is criticized more as an institution than as a faith.

personified.ideology: Obedient faith turning into chosen faith and love
Love as the way to be changed
Lust as power; desire is natural

143516.dominant: Christian (explored and argued with), Expressive individualism (choose your own path), Duty ethics (critiqued), Liberalism (consent and bodily autonomy).

56441.heading: MAOYU: Archenemy and Hero "Be Mine, Hero!" "I Refuse!"
56441.label: From summaries
56441.life_message: Knowledge, honest work and the courage to choose your own fate build a more lasting peace than any victory in battle; people are not insects, and no one has the right to take their freedom.

delivery.evidence: Characters explain each reform and the causes of war at length (anime ep. 1, 6); Kotaku calls the anime mostly characters talking about economics; opponents (Central, the Church) are given motives (dependency, power) but are drawn as villains.
delivery.note: The message is stated rather than inferred, in lecture-like dialogue that began as a play script.

personified.ideology: Peace through knowledge and economic reform
The warrior who learns to fight with ideas
Religious fanaticism and lust for power

56441.dominant: Liberalism (natural rights and the end of serfdom), Pragmatism (reform judged by results), Secular humanism and Progressivism (knowledge and reform as the road to peace).

147329.heading: Marriage Toxin
147329.label: From summaries
147329.life_message: Love is learned by caring for others and becoming someone worth choosing; a man raised to kill can grow toward an ordinary, happy life by protecting people instead of hurting them, and no one should be forced into marriage or childbearing.

content.framing: Action heroics; cruelty condemned; the hero increasingly avoids killing
Shown with consequences; life chosen over death

delivery.evidence: Villains such as Dogo and Byakko get sympathetic backstories (anime ep. 11-12), and Teruaki's case for duty over marriage is heard (ch. 50-52); the clan's view of marriage as breeding is never given a fair defense.
delivery.note: The message about healthy love and consent comes through Mei's coaching and Gero's choices, mixed into fast action and comedy; director Hori says the queer elements are woven in naturally rather than as a big statement (Aftermath).

personified.ideology: Protecting others; love as something earned and chosen

147329.dominant: Expressive individualism, Traditionalism (critiqued: clan duty and forced marriage), Might makes right (critiqued), Communitarianism.

30443.heading: Mars
30443.label: From summaries
30443.life_message: Love that is patient and faithful can help two wounded people heal, if both face the past honestly and choose life over the pull of violence and despair.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; Rei's rage critiqued
Abuse and harassment condemned; teen sex shown as loving and not judged

delivery.evidence: Thompson calls it a tightly plotted romance that handles powerful issues without being preachy or patronizing (via Wikipedia); Garrity says it treats abuse, suicide and murder realistically rather than melodramatically.
delivery.note: The message is carried by the couple's slow changes and by contrast characters (Sei, Masao) rather than by stated lessons.

personified.ideology: Live fast; protect with force; learning to love
Violence and destruction as the only truth

30443.dominant: Secular humanism, Existentialism, Pacifism / nonviolence (personal), Expressive individualism.

86969.heading: Master Magic Efficiently
86969.label: From summaries
86969.life_message: Know what you are truly good at and spend your time on it, and do not try to grow alone: a second chance is best used with friends.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: The lesson is in the premise (the talent-measuring spell) and is carried by action; no source mentions speeches.
delivery.note: A light adventure; the message is structural rather than stated.

86969.dominant: Pragmatism (efficiency and evidence), Communitarianism (the guild over solitary striving).

109900.heading: May I Ask for One Final Thing?
109900.label: From summaries
109900.life_message: No one has to swallow abuse in silence: those who lie, exploit and enslave should be exposed and stopped, and a woman may fight back on her own terms.

content.framing: Endorsed (aimed at villains; played for comic catharsis)

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe the noble villains as cartoonish targets (A.V. Club; ANN ep. 12 calls Terenezza too stupid to see her plan fail); the moral (slavery is wrong, abusers deserve punishment) is never argued against.
delivery.note: The message is carried by comedy and fights rather than speeches; the one serious counter-voice is Leonardo, who warns that her powers cannot always save her (ep. 7).

personified.ideology: the wronged fight back against abusers

109900.dominant: Feminism (a woman refusing abuse), Expressive individualism (dropping the composed mask), Critical theory (punching up at an exploitative aristocracy), Pagan/occult (gods who grant powers).

51860.heading: Mayo Chiki!
51860.label: From summaries
51860.life_message: Be honest about who you are and what you feel; true friends keep your secrets, accept your weaknesses and help you heal.

content.framing: Comic (slapstick); family abuse played as backstory gag
Shown with consequences; resolved by friendship

delivery.evidence: The message comes through the romance plot and the final confessions, not through speeches. Kanade's sadism is treated as charm, and the critics' objections (consent, sexualization) are not voiced inside the story.
delivery.note: Comedy first; the series turns sincere only in volumes 6-7.

51860.dominant: Expressive individualism (being honest about who you are), Communitarianism (found family), Traditionalism (explored: the hereditary butler role).

31211.heading: Me and the Devil Blues: The Unreal Life of Robert Johnson
31211.label: From summaries
31211.life_message: A gift bought at the crossroads costs what you love most, and in the Jim Crow South a Black man's talent and life are never safe.

content.framing: Condemned (racist violence); outlaw violence shown as thrilling and dangerous

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe sparse text and scratchy, atmospheric art that lets music and mood carry the story (Mania); the racism is shown, not lectured (Goboiano).
delivery.note: The moral of the bargain is told through consequences, not speeches; the portrayal of Black characters is itself disputed by critics.

31211.dominant: Pagan/occult (explored), Might makes right (critiqued), Expressive individualism, Critical theory (race critique).

134369.heading: Medaka Kuroiwa Is Impervious to My Charms
134369.label: From summaries
134369.life_message: Real love means letting your true self be seen rather than collecting admiration; the series plays a young monk's vow against teenage romance for comedy, honoring his decency and self-control while treating the rule itself as an obstacle to be tested.

delivery.evidence: Medaka's vow is defended by his own behavior and questioned by friends and Anri; neither side lectures (Japanese Wikipedia; ep. 4).
delivery.note: A comedy without speeches: the message emerges from Mona's gradual honesty and Medaka's decency, not from argument.

personified.ideology: Status through being adored, then sincere love

134369.dominant: Buddhist ideas (a monk-in-training's precept), Expressive individualism (true self over persona), Duty ethics (keeping a vow).

118371.heading: Medalist
118371.label: From summaries
118371.life_message: It is never too late to pour your whole heart into what you love, and the adults who coach children must believe in them, protect them, and not load their own regrets onto them.

content.framing: Neutral (sports injuries); anger shown as a fault

delivery.evidence: Jun Yodaka's win-at-all-costs view is given real weight and real success; Inori's mother's caution is treated as love; Koichi's counsel in ch. 60 is the most openly stated lesson.
delivery.note: The message is carried by training, competition and character backstories rather than speeches, with a few explicit talks from mentors.

personified.ideology: Encouraging, self-giving coaching; never too late
Wholehearted love of the ice; persistence
Talent proven only by winning; sacrifice for victory
Do not sort people into good and evil; share burdens

118371.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Expressive individualism, Duty ethics (promises).

31695.heading: Message to Adolf
31695.label: From summaries
31695.life_message: Hatred taught as an ideology can turn a loving child into a killer and friends into enemies, and "justice" pursued as revenge only hands the killing to the next generation; the story mourns the ordinary people crushed between nations and asks the reader to remember.

content.framing: Condemned (war, persecution and revenge shown as destruction); the hero's fights shown as necessary

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: Kaufmann's rape condemned by the story; Toge's rape followed by consequences but never repented

delivery.evidence: Reviewers call the anti-war message strong but carried by characters and history (Experiments in Manga); the frame story and the closing question about "justice" state it outright (BookDragon; Wikipedia). Nazi ideology is shown from inside a sympathetic child, while Hitler himself is a caricature (TV Tropes).
delivery.note: The message is mostly dramatized, but the ending steps forward to state it, and the cycle-of-revenge coda is the story's argument made plain.

personified.ideology: Jewish identity and friendship; later revenge
Military honor and duty to the state

31695.dominant: Collectivism/authoritarianism (Critiqued), Patriotism / nationalism (Critiqued: ethnic and militarist forms), Pacifism / nonviolence (anti-war), Secular humanism.

86303.heading: Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid
86303.label: From summaries
86303.life_message: A family is something you build by choosing to care for each other, and even beings who began as strangers or enemies can make a home together through patience and everyday kindness.

content.framing: Mixed: same-sex romance affirmed; fan service and child-related gags played as comedy

delivery.evidence: The anti-human views of Ilulu and Tohru's father are given reasons and backstory, and both change by experience rather than lecture (fan wiki). ANN's Peralta reads the themes as carried by everyday comedy.
delivery.note: Tolerance and chosen family are shown in daily life; Kobayashi occasionally states her view plainly, but the series rarely preaches.

personified.ideology: Devotion; learning to live among humans
Dragon supremacy, then love of humans

86303.dominant: Communitarianism (found family), Progressivism (a same-sex couple made ordinary), Secular humanism, Expressive individualism.

111149.heading: Mission: Yozakura Family
111149.label: From summaries
111149.life_message: Family is the people who will protect you whatever it costs; love, loyalty and a refusal to kill can stand against those who treat people as tools.

content.framing: Action-adventure; cruelty and experimentation condemned; the hero refuses to kill

delivery.evidence: Villains get backstories (Mizuki lost his family to pollution; Akai to arson; Asa began by trying to save lives), but their methods are plainly condemned; the family rule against killing is stated and tested.
delivery.note: The family theme is spoken often (Kyoichiro tells Taiyo that family is the one thing you can trust, per the fan wiki) but carried mostly by action and comedy.

personified.ideology: Sacrifice individuals for the greater good

111149.dominant: Communitarianism (family first), Traditionalism (marriage, lineage, children), Pacifism / nonviolence (Taiyo's no-kill rule), Utilitarianism (critiqued in Asa).

149893.heading: Mistress Kanan Is Devilishly Easy
149893.label: From summaries
149893.life_message: Love and small shared joys, like eating croquettes together, can change even a demon's appetites, and a family's blessing is worth earning with patience and courage.

delivery.evidence: The moral (love and shared meals change you) is stated once by Beelzebub's lesson (ep. 1) and otherwise shown through gags.
delivery.note: The message is carried by episodic comedy, not argument.

149893.dominant: Hedonism (desire and food as comedy), Pagan/occult (a demon family as heroes), Communitarianism (winning a family's blessing).

30214.heading: Mobile Suit Gundam: The Origin
30214.label: From summaries
30214.life_message: War devours the young and the ordinary while the powerful play for power; a good life holds on to the people beside you and refuses to let war or revenge make you into a weapon.

content.framing: Mixed: romance shown warmly; abuse and attempted assault condemned

30214.dominant: Collectivism/authoritarianism, Patriotism / nationalism, Might makes right, Pacifism / nonviolence.

delivery.evidence: ANN says both sides are shown with human emotions; reviewers praise the storytelling and no one calls it preachy (ANN; SLJ; Otaku USA).
delivery.note: Ideas are carried by characters and events: Gihren's speeches, Degwin's doubts, Tianem's mercy and Char's revenge argue with one another without a narrator's verdict.

66213.heading: Monster Musume
66213.label: From summaries
66213.life_message: Kindness and acceptance can make a home for anyone, however strange, and prejudice is the real monster; the series delivers this through constant sexual comedy in which consent is often treated as a joke.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy; non-consent often played for laughs; villains' assaults condemned

delivery.evidence: The racist couple are cartoon villains with no case (ch. 2, 9); prejudice is never given a fair hearing. The anti-prejudice message is carried by situations, not speeches.
delivery.note: Acceptance is the stated theme, but the sexual comedy dominates almost every chapter.

personified.ideology: Distrust born of abuse, healed by acceptance

66213.dominant: Hedonism (affirmed), Communitarianism (found family), acceptance of the outsider through Progressivism and Liberalism (explored).

30001.heading: Monster
30001.label: From summaries
30001.life_message: Every life has equal worth, even a monster's: a good person keeps saving lives rather than taking one, and a name, a memory and someone who cares are what keep a person human.

delivery.evidence: Characters argue the worth of a life directly (Tenma, Eva, Johan); TV Tropes lists forgiveness as the moral; no review opened calls it preachy.
delivery.note: Competing views on the worth of a life are voiced by characters within a thriller plot, and the villain's view gets a full, frightening hearing.

personified.ideology: Death is the only equality; nihilism

30001.dominant: Nihilism (critiqued), Duty ethics (affirmed), Secular humanism, Existentialism, Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Communitarianism.

59211.heading: Monthly Girls' Nozaki-kun
59211.label: From summaries
59211.life_message: Real people are kinder, stranger and funnier than the romance clichés we expect of them; friends who help each other and accept each other's quirks are worth more than a story-book love.

delivery.evidence: Four-panel gags with no lectures; the gender-role commentary is carried by reversals and misunderstandings (The Mary Sue; Anime Feminist).
delivery.note: Its outlook comes through parody of romance-manga clichés and the friend group's comedy, not through speeches.

personified.ideology: Gender roles as a costume one may enjoy

59211.dominant: Postmodernism (genre parody and metafiction), Communitarianism (the friend group), Expressive individualism.

136253.heading: Monthly in the Garden with My Landlord
136253.label: From summaries
136253.life_message: After a hurtful relationship, a calm home, honest conversation and caring for each other can grow into a real partnership; love means both giving care and letting yourself receive it.

delivery.evidence: The values come through daily scenes and calm talks (Okazu); family questions are raised gently and taken seriously (vol. 4-5).
delivery.note: No one lectures; doubts from parents and grandparents are treated as fair concerns to answer.

136253.dominant: Expressive individualism (choosing one's own life and partner); Communitarianism (friends and both families); Progressivism (an affirmed same-sex couple).

98544.heading: Moriarty the Patriot
98544.label: From summaries
98544.life_message: Cruel privilege deserves to fall, but the man who kills to bring it down still carries real guilt: death is no atonement, and friendship gives him a reason to live and make amends.

content.framing: Mixed: murders of cruel nobles framed as justice; the nobles' own cruelty and the Ripper killings condemned

content.frequency: Builds through the story; peaks at the climax

delivery.evidence: The Beat's Santilli finds Moriarty not sanitized, his methods cruel enough to frighten; WWAC finds the noble targets classist to an implausible degree. Holmes and Watson argue against William at length (ch. 55, 66).
delivery.note: The class critique is built into every case, while the counterargument (no one may decide who dies) is carried by Holmes and lands at the climax.

personified.ideology: Ending the class system by any means
Truth; no one may decide who dies

98544.dominant: Utilitarianism (ends versus means, explored), Duty ethics (Holmes's counterweight), Critical theory and Marxism (class critique), Patriotism (remaking the nation the hero loves).

30740.heading: MPD Psycho
30740.label: From summaries
30740.life_message: A self can be copied, programmed and used by people with power, so no one simply owns their soul; what survives is the choice to protect someone else's.

content.framing: Condemned in plot, but displayed in lavish detail

delivery.evidence: No narrator judges the killers or the conspiracy; CBR says the psychology of identity is underexplored, and ANN says the ideas are carried by plot reveals.
delivery.note: The theme of manipulated identity comes through twists and reveals rather than statements; Shinji, a killer, is drawn as charismatic rather than as a lesson.

personified.ideology: Persons as engineered material for power

30740.dominant: Postmodernism (the self as constructed), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Transhumanism (critiqued), Nihilism.

123625.heading: Mr. Paper Bag is in Love
123625.label: From summaries
123625.life_message: Sincere, patient kindness matters more than looks or first impressions, and being accepted as you are can give a very shy person the courage to be seen.

content.framing: Mixed (played as sweet; the friend calls it stalking)

delivery.evidence: The friend voices the stalker worry openly before being reassured (MyAnimeList synopsis); the message is carried by comedy and small acts, not speeches.
delivery.note: An author's note at the start says the aim is simply to make readers' hearts feel warm (MyAnimeList review, paraphrased).

personified.ideology: Love sincerely even when you cannot show your face

123625.dominant: Expressive individualism (gently); no lens is strong in this light romance.

107275.heading: Mr. Villain's Day Off
107275.label: From summaries
107275.life_message: Rest, small pleasures and simple courtesy matter: a person who guards his days off and treats everyone decently, even his enemies, is happier and kinder for it.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: The message is shown through gags about the General's rules and outings; Anime Feminist calls the work-life balance focus a "constructive fantasy." Both the villains and the Rangers are drawn as decent people.
delivery.note: No lectures; the values sit in what the General does on his days off.

107275.dominant: Communitarianism (enemies become friends), Expressive individualism (self-care), Hedonism (small pleasures, mild).

151444.heading: Mujina into the Deep
151444.label: From summaries
151444.life_message: When a society puts human rights up for sale, the people it throws away can still choose to protect one another; a found family can give back the humanity a cruel system takes.

content.framing: Mixed: the heroine's killing is her trade and is not judged; cruelty by exploiters and the state is condemned
Mixed: sexual exploitation of a minor and of children is condemned; adult sex and sex work are shown frankly and not judged

delivery.evidence: The critique is built into the setting (rights cards, the 85-year cutoff, Division 9) rather than argued in speeches; The Outer Haven praises Asano's familiar blunt dialogue and dark humor (vol. 2).
delivery.note: The state and the brokers are not given a sympathetic case in sources opened, but police officer Kashio and broker Nive are drawn as mixed people.

personified.ideology: rightless survival through skill; feelings as weakness
influencer fame and violence as content

151444.dominant: Liberalism (rights and consent), Critical theory, Authoritarianism (critiqued), Communitarianism (found family), Strength rules (explored).

95098.heading: Multi-Mind Mayhem: Isekai Tensei Soudouki
95098.label: From summaries
95098.life_message: Knowledge, hard work and courage, shared with loyal friends and family, can build prosperity and protect the people you are responsible for.

delivery.evidence: The story shows inventions and victories rather than arguing for them; enemies are mostly schemers or invaders (One Peace Books synopses; ANN).
delivery.note: A power fantasy whose values (stewardship, family, loyalty) are carried by plot, with little debate.

personified.ideology: Knowledge and enterprise for the common good
The samurai's love of battle and money
Modern knowledge; the present life matters most

95098.dominant: Pragmatism (modern know-how solves problems), Bushido / honor code (the samurai soul), Patriotism (defending Mauricia and Antrim), Communitarianism (a lord building his domain with loyal people).

85281.heading: MURCIÉLAGO
85281.label: From summaries
85281.life_message: In a city overrun by killers, it takes a monster to stop monsters: the story enjoys its psychopathic heroine's freedom and appetites, gives her a protective love for the girls in her care, and asks little about whether licensed killing is justice.

content.framing: Endorsed when Kuroko kills killers; villains' cruelty condemned

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Endorsed (adult sex as part of Kuroko's freedom); the abuse of minors by villains condemned, but the heroine's interest in children played as comedy
Condemned (the drug is the villains' weapon)

delivery.evidence: No character argues against the executioner bargain; villains are given tragic pasts in bonus pages (TV Tropes) but are killed. ANN notes the humor keeps the dark material relatively light.
delivery.note: The view is carried by Kuroko's swagger and the comedy; the story does not reflect on its premise.

85281.dominant: Hedonism (Kuroko's appetites), Might makes right (the strongest killer wins), Utilitarianism (the executioner bargain), Expressive individualism (an unapologetic self).

30418.heading: Mushishi
30418.label: From summaries
30418.life_message: People belong to a larger living world they cannot master; meet what you do not understand with patient knowledge and compassion, accept loss, and seek balance instead of blame.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: Ginko states his view that mushi are not evil (Wikipedia), but most stories do not center him; people make their own choices and live with them, and hard dilemmas (ch. 13) are left open.
delivery.note: The message lives in the shape of each story and Ginko's quiet example, not in speeches.

personified.ideology: Duty carried with love for what harms her
Sacrifice of one for the many

113168.heading: My Alcoholic Escape from Reality
113168.label: From summaries
113168.life_message: Running from pain into drink breaks the body as well as the mind; recovery is slow and untidy, but honesty, the care of others and work you believe in can lead back to life.

delivery.evidence: She addresses readers directly in a chapter-length aside on why she drinks (Ani-Gamers); the book argues with itself about whether to write memoir at all (Real Sound).
delivery.note: A diary comic that tells its lesson openly but without lecturing; it admits alcohol's appeal and her own lapses.

personified.ideology: Escape through drink; then honest self-facing
Shame at public exposure; family care

113168.dominant: Existentialism; Expressive individualism (honest self-expression); Hedonism critiqued.

104699.heading: My Androgynous Boyfriend
104699.label: From summaries
104699.life_message: Love means supporting your partner as they are: how a man dresses or wears makeup says nothing about his love or his worth, and a couple can make its own kind of happiness.

delivery.evidence: The message comes through everyday chapters and misunderstanding jokes; Silverman says the gender issues are raised but not explored.
delivery.note: A light slice-of-life romance; no character argues for traditional gender roles at length in sources opened.

personified.ideology: Gender expression is personal; devoted love

104699.dominant: Expressive individualism, Progressivism (gender expression), Consumerism (fashion and social media).

114437.heading: My Awkward Senpai
114437.label: From summaries
114437.life_message: A hard shell often hides a frightened, caring person, and patience and kindness can draw them out; love grows slowly between equals who learn to be honest.

delivery.evidence: A short-chapter romantic comedy; ANN describes themes of workaholism, fear of emotional dependency and adults not having everything figured out, carried by gags rather than speeches.
delivery.note: There is no ideological conflict; the message about kindness and honesty is shown through small scenes.

personified.ideology: Protect yourself behind a strict front
Playful honesty; push friends toward their feelings

114437.dominant: Gentle workplace romance; showing your true self; senior-junior duty and kindness.

98858.heading: My Boy
98858.label: From summaries
98858.life_message: Two lonely people can give each other what they lack, but an adult must be honest about what her attachment to a child really is and must not act on it; the story insists on that line and leaves their future open.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Explored; the adult's restraint is upheld, but the attachment is drawn with sympathy and the ending is open

delivery.evidence: Told mainly through Satoko's quiet monologue (Japanese Wikipedia), with some chapters from other viewpoints; the father, the company and Nao voice the outside world's objections.
delivery.note: The story asks rather than tells: Anime UK News says Takano does not ask readers to condemn her characters.

98858.dominant: Existentialism (loneliness and self-deception), Duty ethics (the line an adult must not cross), Expressive individualism.

93006.heading: My Brother's Husband
93006.label: From summaries
93006.life_message: Family is made by love and acceptance; quiet, everyday prejudice wounds both the people it targets and the people who hold it, and it can be unlearned.

content.framing: Endorsed: same-sex marriage and gay identity affirmed; nudity non-sexual

delivery.evidence: NPR says Tagame clearly has an agenda but finds Yaichi's obstacles realistic; AniList tags it Educational (80%); ANN praises it as emotional without manipulation; the split thought-and-speech panels show the traditional reflex from inside.
delivery.note: The traditional view lives mainly inside Yaichi and is treated with sympathy as he changes; outside objectors (Yuki's mother, the teacher) are brief and shown as mistaken. Kana's questions and Mike's answers sometimes work as lessons to the reader.

personified.ideology: Quiet, implicit discomfort with homosexuality, later overcome
Open acceptance of gay identity and same-sex marriage
Gay adults as a bad influence on children
Homosexuality as a subject for adults, not for school

93006.dominant: Progressivism, Liberalism (equal rights and marriage), Communitarianism (family and neighborhood), Expressive individualism.

86833.heading: My Capricorn friend
86833.label: From summaries
86833.life_message: Staying silent while a classmate is tormented is itself a choice with a cost; standing beside a friend, even late, matters, and guilt and innocence are rarely as simple as they first look.

delivery.evidence: A MAL reviewer sums up the message as bullying is wrong and bystanders should step in, carried by Yūya's guilt and choices rather than lectures; Naoto's survival creed is given its own voice in the blurb.
delivery.note: The message is clear but carried by a mystery plot; how sympathetically Naoto's creed is treated at the end is to verify.

personified.ideology: No one helps the bullied, so one must act alone to survive

86833.dominant: Existentialism (choice and guilt), Might makes right (critiqued), Duty ethics (explored).

156867.heading: My Crush's Crush
156867.label: From summaries
156867.life_message: Feelings don't always point back at us; being honest about what you feel, and kind when it isn't returned, keeps friendships alive through heartbreak.

delivery.evidence: A farce of crossing crushes; no character argues a worldview. The author describes it as a lighthearted, soothing everyday comedy (Web The Television).
delivery.note: Romantic comedy with no message beyond honesty and kindness.

156867.dominant: Expressive individualism (honest feelings), Communitarianism (the club as a small family), Progressivism (a same-sex crush treated as ordinary).

102476.heading: My Daughter Left the Nest and Returned an S-Rank Adventurer: The Black-Haired Valkyrie
102476.label: From summaries
102476.life_message: A loving parent's quiet faithfulness shapes a strong and good child, and true strength is skill used to protect others, kept humble, and always finding its way home.
102476.dominant: Communitarianism, Traditionalism, Classical virtue ethics, Pagan/occult (critiqued).

delivery.evidence: The father-daughter bond and Belgrieve's humility are shown through episodes rather than lectures (ANN; MyAnimeList reviews); villains such as Malta and Francois are drawn as plainly greedy or arrogant.
delivery.note: Warm, low-key slice of life between fantasy battles; its values are carried by Belgrieve's example.

personified.ideology: Humble, faithful service; skill over power
Devotion to family; duty to help others

123181.heading: My Death Flags Show No Sign of Ending
123181.label: From summaries
123181.life_message: Goodness shows in quiet deeds, not words or reputation; a person can refuse the cruel part that fate and family wrote for them.

delivery.evidence: The moral comes through the gap between what Harold says and what he does; his parents are drawn as cartoon snobs (The Outerhaven), while the butler and Erika's father are fair-minded.
delivery.note: No lectures: the comedy of a kind man stuck with a cruel tongue carries the message.

personified.ideology: Quiet goodness behind a villain's manner

123181.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Existentialism (defying fate), Pragmatism.

101583.heading: My Dress-Up Darling
101583.label: From summaries
101583.life_message: A good life comes from loving what you love without shame, doing your craft with care, and being accepted by people who see the real you; mocking someone's passions is the wrong the story sets out to undo.

content.framing: Endorsed (romance; Marin's open enjoyment of adult games); fan service presented as comedy

delivery.evidence: Marin and Wakana state the message about not mocking hobbies; the childhood friend who mocked Wakana is given regret and a reconciliation rather than being a villain.
delivery.note: The acceptance message is spoken openly, carried by comedy and craft detail rather than lectures.

101583.dominant: Expressive individualism, Classical virtue ethics (craft and diligence), Progressivism (gendered hobbies challenged), Communitarianism (the cosplay community).

166929.heading: My Favorite VTuber Is Scary IRL
166929.label: From summaries
166929.life_message: Shy and hurt people can grow, step by step, through patient friendship and honest talk, and nobody should be judged by how they look.

content.framing: Mixed: body-shaming condemned in the story, while the art dwells on her body

delivery.evidence: Siliconera reads each volume as having a theme (anxiety, then communication, then support), carried by small scenes; the leads talk problems out instead of lecturing.
delivery.note: The message is consistent; the main tension is between the story's respect for the heroine and the art's focus on her body.

personified.ideology: Courage to grow despite fear and past harm
Online persona as a cover for loneliness

166929.dominant: Communitarianism (mutual support), Classical virtue ethics (courage in small steps), Expressive individualism, Consumerism (explored).

113961.heading: My Friend's Little Sister Has It in for Me!
113961.label: From summaries
113961.life_message: Misfits who look out for one another can make something worth more than an efficient, lonely life; you show your true self to the people you trust.

delivery.evidence: The message about friendship and dreams is carried by the team's work and Akiteru's choices; Mikawa states the theme as "comrades" who do not fit in (interview). The disapproving mother is mostly an offstage obstacle.
delivery.note: A comedy first; any message comes through character backstories rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: Follow your dream; be yourself with those you trust

113961.dominant: Expressive individualism (dreams against family disapproval), Communitarianism (the found team), Pragmatism (efficiency, softened).

140862.heading: My Girlfriend Cheated on Me, and Now My Flirty Underclassman Won’t Leave Me Alone
140862.label: From summaries
140862.life_message: Heartbreak is not the end: honest friendship and patient, chosen love can rebuild trust, but choosing someone means being honest with everyone who cares for you.

delivery.evidence: The romance carries the message; the ex-girlfriend gets her own account (novel vol. 3; manga vol. 6); the final novel frames choosing someone as choosing a form of happiness (Kadokawa blurb).
delivery.note: Lessons about honesty and faithfulness come through events, not lectures, as far as the blurbs show.

personified.ideology: Love that chases what it wants
The ex whose side is unheard at first

140862.dominant: Expressive individualism (following your heart to the right partner), Classical virtue ethics (honesty and growing worthy), Communitarianism (friends as support).

155228.heading: My Girlfriend is 8 Meters Tall
155228.label: From summaries
155228.life_message: Love sees the person, not the size: caring for someone means helping her live as fully as anyone else.

delivery.evidence: The inclusion theme is shown through daily logistics and friends' help rather than speeches (Japanese Wikipedia; Seven Seas synopses).
delivery.note: No ideology is argued; the comedy carries the message. Manga delivery is judged from summaries only.

155228.dominant: Communitarianism (inclusion), Expressive individualism (a confident, different heroine); Hedonism in the fan service.

177188.heading: My Girlfriend Is a Colossal Cutie
177188.label: From summaries
177188.life_message: Love can turn insecurity about your body into confidence, and a good couple supports each other whatever others might say.

delivery.evidence: The message is carried by the couple's dates and school events; no character argues against them in sources opened (publisher blurbs; reader comments).
delivery.note: A light romantic comedy with no lectures.

177188.dominant: Expressive individualism (self-acceptance), with a light Feminism note (reversed size and strength roles).

169734.heading: My Gyaru Wife's Secrets
169734.label: From summaries
169734.life_message: A marriage is worth protecting and enjoying: a couple who keep choosing each other, playfully and faithfully, find their happiest selves at home together.

delivery.evidence: Billed as a pure love comedy (Mangamo blurb); the message is carried by situations, not speeches (Mangapedia; ciatr).
delivery.note: A romantic comedy without an argued worldview; marriage is shown as the reward, not argued for.

personified.ideology: Devoted love behind a cool public persona

169734.dominant: Hedonism (playful married intimacy), Traditionalism (marriage and home), Expressive individualism (the gyaru self behind the office persona).

106531.heading: My Happy Marriage
106531.label: From summaries
106531.life_message: A person's worth is not set by those who mistreat them; patient kindness and faithful love can heal deep wounds, and a mistreated girl can find her own place and gift.

content.framing: Condemned (family abuse); neutral for supernatural battles

delivery.evidence: The stepfamily is drawn as plainly cruel, though Kiyoka sees Kaya's entitlement as learned from her parents (ch. 16) and Shinichi's backstory explains his coldness (fan wiki). The message comes through Miyo's experience, not speeches.
delivery.note: A Cinderella romance whose values are shown in who is kind and who is cruel; villains get a little background but little defense.

106531.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (affirmed), Traditionalism (explored), Might makes right (critiqued), Confucian ethics.

97842.heading: My Hero Academia: Vigilantes
97842.label: From summaries
97842.life_message: Doing good for the people around you matters more than an official title, but helping outside the rules has real costs, and a true hero protects others without becoming a killer.

content.framing: Mixed: threats condemned; some sexual humor and fan-service design

delivery.evidence: The police detective and licensed pros argue the case for law fairly and help win the day; Knuckleduster's critique of the hero system is heard but not adopted wholesale; the ending gives Koichi real legal consequences (ch. 124).
delivery.note: The theme is carried by action and comedy; ANN's anime reviewer felt the vigilante question is underused early on.

personified.ideology: Do small good deeds, licensed or not
Fix what the system misses, by force
The rule of law, applied humanely
Fame and meaning by any means

97842.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (kindness and courage), Communitarianism (a neighborhood that protects its own), Libertarianism (doing good without a license).

85486.heading: My Hero Academia (Boku no Hero Academia)
85486.label: From summaries
85486.life_message: A good life is spent helping others without being asked, even at cost to yourself; and real heroism means reaching out to save the person no one else will, including the "villain".

content.frequency: Frequent, rising sharply from the Paranormal Liberation War (v26 onward)

content.framing: Mixed: Mineta's behavior is punished or rebuked by classmates; adult heroine costumes are neutral

delivery.evidence: Anime Feminist's Mo Black reads its politics as conservative; Plugged In praises its self-sacrifice message; neither calls it preachy.
delivery.note: Villains such as Shigaraki and Stain state their grievances against hero society directly, and the story answers mainly through Deku; the final chapter states the theme in Deku's own reflections (ch. 430).

personified.ideology: A society that failed a child deserves destruction
Only true heroes deserve the name

85486.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Might makes right (critiqued), Secular humanism, Critical theory (contested), Duty ethics.

108196.heading: My Home Hero
108196.label: From summaries
108196.life_message: A father's love can drive an ordinary man to terrible acts; protecting your family is right, but each crime breeds more crimes, more guilt and more danger, and the story keeps asking whether a good dad who has killed can ever be forgiven.

content.framing: Mixed: the father's killing framed as desperate protection with lasting guilt; gang and cult violence condemned

delivery.evidence: Readers disagree whether the story endorses Tetsuo (MyAnimeList reviews); guilt and confession are shown rather than preached (Apple Books vol. 17; Kodansha vol. 10); chapter titles name the themes directly ("My Sin," "Atonement," "A Good Dad").
delivery.note: The moral question is carried by plot consequences and Tetsuo's guilt; villains are drawn as cruel, but Matori is given a father's grief that mirrors Tetsuo's.

personified.ideology: Protect your family at any cost

108196.dominant: Utilitarianism (killing to save), Communitarianism (family first), Duty ethics (law, confession and atonement), Collectivism/authoritarianism (the cult, critiqued).

101584.heading: My Instant Death Ability is So Overpowered, No One in This Other World Stands a Chance Against Me! —AΩ—
101584.label: From summaries
101584.life_message: Power is safest with someone who was taught restraint and cares about one person; those who use power to abandon, dominate or prey on others end up destroyed by it.

content.framing: Endorsed as just deserts for attackers; the Sage's and classmates' cruelty condemned
Mixed: teasing fan service played for comedy; sexual threats and coercion condemned and punished

delivery.evidence: ANN Preview Guide critics: the classmates become cruel for no particular reason, so their deaths feel deserved; no serious case is made for the Sage or the enslavers. Tomochika's objections are the only internal check.
delivery.note: The story rarely argues; it sets up cartoonishly cruel villains and lets the hero end them. The satire tag (AniList) depends on reading that as parody of the genre.

personified.ideology: Indifferent, overwhelming power, restrained by one rule
Power used for cruelty and domination

101584.dominant: Strength rules (explored), Absurdism and satire, Duty ethics (Yogiri's one rule), Authoritarianism (critiqued).

106144.heading: My Isekai Life: I Gained a Second Character Class and Became the Strongest Sage in the World!
106144.label: From summaries
106144.life_message: Quiet, careful competence used to protect ordinary people matters more than fame or reward, and a life swallowed by overwork is no life at all.

content.framing: Neutral (fantasy action); killing of monsters celebrated, killing of people avoided
Shown as fanaticism; not dwelt on

delivery.evidence: No speeches about the message; Yuji simply refuses credit and helps. Walter is given a motive (cleansing sin) but no argument, and Silverman (ANN) found the cult no real threat; Yuji answers the Sage only that he likes the world as it is (ep. 12, Wikipedia summary).
delivery.note: A light power fantasy; the overwork satire lives in flashbacks and Yuji's habits rather than in dialogue.

personified.ideology: Quiet competence; protect people without seeking credit
Faith in revelation and church duty
Religious fanaticism: cleanse the world of sin by destroying people

106144.dominant: Pragmatism, Communitarianism, Classical virtue ethics (humility), with fantasy magic as setting.

193817.heading: My Life Turned Around: After I Was Betrayed and Framed, I Won the Heart of the Most Beautiful Girl at School
193817.label: From summaries
193817.life_message: Lies and betrayal eventually come to light, and a person at the bottom can be lifted up by one act of kindness, especially when he also saves someone else.

delivery.evidence: The wrongdoers are drawn as selfish or scheming; the story's sympathy is clear from the title on (publisher blurb; chapter titles such as "The Darkness of the Childhood Friend").
delivery.note: A genre melodrama of betrayal and vindication; the message comes through plot, not speeches.

193817.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (honesty rewarded), Communitarianism (adults and family as protectors), Liberalism (fair process against mob judgment).

109921.heading: My Love Mix-Up!
109921.label: From summaries
109921.life_message: Love can surprise you; honesty and kindness, not labels, are what make it real, and friends who accept you make it easier to be yourself.

content.framing: Endorsed (same-sex teen romance presented as good)

delivery.evidence: The acceptance theme rides on comedy and character choices (VIZ synopses); MangaUpdates tags Homophobia and LGBT Issues, so some prejudiced views appear, but no source describes how they are drawn (to verify). No review on delivery could be opened.
delivery.note: The message is carried by a comedy of misunderstandings and a slow, sweet romance rather than by speeches.

109921.dominant: Progressivism (affirming same-sex love), Expressive individualism (self-discovery), Communitarianism (accepting friends).

66933.heading: My Love Story!!
66933.label: From summaries
66933.life_message: Kindness, honesty and loyalty matter more than looks, a true friend is worth as much as a sweetheart, and love grows by putting the other person's good first.

delivery.evidence: The message (character over looks) is the premise and the running joke; rivals like Ichinose are given their own sincere view (Wikipedia; VIZ vols. 9-10).
delivery.note: Takeo's goodness is shown in action and played for comedy rather than preached.

personified.ideology: Loyal friendship; judge people by how they treat others
Looks and talent as the measure of a match

66933.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (kindness, courage, loyalty), Communitarianism (friends and family), Confucian ethics (honor to parents).

112222.heading: My Lovey-Dovey Wife is a Stone Cold Killer
112222.label: From summaries
112222.life_message: A marriage grows warm through daily care, patience and acceptance, and love can soften even a cold and dangerous person; the story keeps her killing offstage as a running joke.

content.framing: Neutral (killing as a comic job; victims unseen)

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Endorsed (married romance; fan service as part of the appeal)

delivery.evidence: Episodic romantic comedy (Seven Seas synopses for vols. 1-8; Wikipedia); no message is argued, and the killing is never debated.
delivery.note: A situational romantic comedy that does not argue for any worldview; its implied message is about acceptance in marriage.

personified.ideology: Devotion to husband and home; killing as a job

112222.dominant: Traditionalism (marriage, homemaking and the extended family), Communitarianism (family and neighbors), with killing as a background gag.

85139.heading: My Monster Secret: Actually, I Am…
85139.label: From summaries
85139.life_message: Honesty, keeping your word and accepting people who are different let love and friendship grow; humans and 'monsters' can share one school and one future.

content.framing: Played for comedy; harassment mostly unjudged

delivery.evidence: The honesty and coexistence themes come through gags and the final arc; the separatist Shirayuki is given a painful backstory (fan wiki).
delivery.note: Its message is carried by comedy and a late dramatic turn rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: Honesty; keeping promises at any cost
Living openly as who you are

85139.dominant: Duty ethics (honesty and promise-keeping), Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism.
