delivery.evidence: ANN: the friendship is a real goal, and the late revelations are both funny and moving. The author says she lets characters on opposing sides look for a compromise inside the story (Japanese Wikipedia, Comic Space interview).
delivery.note: Each four-panel strip has a punchline, while each volume quietly sets up and resolves a larger mystery; the message of coexistence is acted out, not lectured.

107462.dominant: Communitarianism (protecting the town together), Pacifism / nonviolence (an enemy who cannot hurt anyone), Pagan/occult (demons and spirits as fantasy).

66723.heading: The Devil Is a Part-Timer!
66723.label: From summaries
66723.life_message: Who you are is shown by how you work and how you care for the people in front of you, not by the title or label the world gave you: even a "devil" can change, and power that hides behind holiness can be the real evil.

content.framing: Mixed: the heroes' fights defensive and celebrated; the Church's and angels' violence condemned

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: romance chaste; fan service played as comedy

delivery.evidence: Emi's view that demons are simply evil is given weight and only slowly answered; but the Church's leaders and the angels are drawn as schemers with few redeeming traits.
delivery.note: The message comes through comedy (a devil-king fry cook) and through who keeps faith with whom, with occasional speeches against the angels (ch. 78, 96).

66723.dominant: Pragmatism (honest work and competence), Communitarianism (a found family of former enemies), Christian (its institutions and angels inverted and critiqued), Pagan/occult (demons, magic and holy power as fantasy furniture).

30970.heading: The Drifting Classroom
30970.label: From summaries
30970.life_message: Even when the adults fail and the world is ruined by human greed, children who refuse to sacrifice one another, own their wrongs and keep faith with those who love them can begin again; the future can still be changed if people change now.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; cruelty by adults and tyrants condemned

delivery.evidence: Umezu says he wove the social issues of the 1970s into a children's adventure (Dazed); the mutants show the children a film about overpopulation and pollution (vol. 8, EBSCO), the most direct statement. Otomo's ruthless pragmatism gets a fair hearing; Sekiya and Princess are drawn as monsters.
delivery.note: The message comes through events and choices more than speeches, though the environmental warning becomes explicit near the end.

personified.ideology: Protect everyone; no one is expendable

30970.dominant: Environmentalism, Communitarianism, Duty ethics (no one may be sacrificed), Might makes right (critiqued).

100293.heading: The Duke of Death and His Maid
100293.label: From summaries
100293.life_message: Faithful love that stays close despite the cost, and kindness even toward the one who did the harm, can break a curse of isolation.

content.framing: Endorsed as affectionate comedy; mutual attraction; no sex

delivery.evidence: The villain Sade is given a lonely, sympathetic inner life and is redeemed; the mother's rejection is explained rather than condemned (fan wiki). The message of faithful love is carried by daily episodes, not speeches.
delivery.note: Episodic comedy carries the romance; the final arc turns to forgiveness and reconciliation.

100293.dominant: Communitarianism (a found family of servants, siblings and witches), Pagan/occult (witches and curses as the world), with virtue-centered faithful love and a choice of love over station.

87234.heading: The Elder Sister-Like One
87234.label: From summaries
87234.life_message: Being loved and belonging to someone is worth almost any price; a family can be made, even with something not human, though the bargain may cost more than it seems.

content.framing: Neutral; horror mostly softened by comedy

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Endorsed as appealing; sexual content involving a minor

delivery.evidence: No message is stated; the longing for family is carried by Yuu's wish and daily life with Chiyo (Wikipedia; The Fandom Post). The relatives are drawn only as cold.
delivery.note: Warmth and fan service are delivered together; the cost of the pact is hinted at through ominous narration rather than argued (The Fandom Post, vol. 2).

personified.ideology: Grief that tries to undo death

87234.dominant: Pagan/occult (a summoned deity as guardian), Communitarianism (a made family), Hedonism (fan service).

128666.heading: The Elusive Samurai
128666.label: From summaries
128666.life_message: There can be honor in surviving: running to live and to protect others can take more courage than a glorious death, and a life spent for the people you love matters more than revenge.

content.framing: Mixed: battles played as thrilling action; cruelty and tyranny condemned
Neutral; the rape in a backstory is condemned

content.frequency: Occasional, heavy at the start and end
content.framing: Shown with consequences; honorable suicide questioned

delivery.evidence: Warriors who prefer death are given their reasons before being persuaded (ch. 26-31); villains are often grotesque "oni," but several (Shokan, Ogasawara, Kiyohara) get backstories and respect.
delivery.note: The message is shown in action and comedy; Hongo's history notes add context without moralizing.

personified.ideology: Survival and protection over honorable death
Charismatic power without reason or loyalty
Faith and foresight in service of the weak

128666.dominant: Bushido / honor code (critiqued: survival over glorious death), Pragmatism (flight as strategy), Confucian ethics (loyalty and gratitude), Might makes right (critiqued).

112978.heading: The Enigma of Amigara Fault
112978.label: From summaries
112978.life_message: No life message is offered; the story pictures a compulsion that draws people to their own destruction, even when they know where it leads.

delivery.evidence: Ito says the story grew from one image and his questions about it (ANN interview); critics supply the readings (ANN feature; CBR), and the text states no lesson.
delivery.note: The meaning is left entirely to the reader; the only contrary voice, Owaki's early skepticism, is overtaken by events.

112978.dominant: Nihilism, Existentialism, Absurdism (as explored, not endorsed).

109406.heading: The Evening and The Sea
109406.label: From summaries
109406.life_message: Opening up to one other person can bring color to a guarded life, and caring for someone can mean letting her go to grow.

delivery.evidence: The creator says the sea scenes carry feelings that people rarely say aloud (Manga-Passion); reviewers note the story leaves gaps for the reader to fill (Okazu, vol. 1).
delivery.note: Feelings are carried by images of fish and the sea rather than by speeches.

109406.dominant: Expressive individualism (quiet), Existentialism (choosing to care), Buddhist ideas as an echo (impermanence and letting go).

123582.heading: The Executed Sage Who Was Reincarnated as a Lich Started an All-Out War
123582.label: From summaries
123582.life_message: A betrayed hero takes on the role of the world's villain so that warring nations will unite against him; peace, the story suggests, may be bought by one person carrying the world's hatred and guilt.

content.framing: Mixed: the hero's wars presented as necessary; cruelty for pleasure condemned

delivery.evidence: Readers note Dwight's speeches about the world being wrong and his theatrical "against the world" moments, and that nearly all human leaders are power-hungry villains (MyAnimeList reviews).
delivery.note: The thesis is stated by the hero; opponents are mostly drawn as corrupt, so the story rarely tests his view against a fair one.

personified.ideology: Peace through conquest; bearing the world's hatred
Power and fear of the strong

personified.character: The Saint of the holy army
The new Hero with holy magic
personified.ideology: Righteous resistance to the Demon Lord

123582.dominant: Utilitarianism (peace by any means), Might makes right, Pagan/occult (necromancy), Collectivism/authoritarianism.

150193.heading: The Exiled Heavy Knight Knows How to Game the System
150193.label: From summaries
150193.life_message: What others call a weakness can be a strength if you understand it and work at it; worth is proved by what you do with patience, knowledge and a trusted partner, not by the label you were given.

delivery.evidence: Snobs and cheats (Teal, Cline, Matilda) are quickly humbled (a MyAnimeList reviewer notes antagonists are quickly humbled); Elymas's inner monologue explains each lesson.
delivery.note: The message that labels lie is built into every fight and spelled out in Elymas's narration, but carried by action rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: Worth by class and family prestige

150193.dominant: Pragmatism, Classical virtue ethics (perseverance and courage), Traditionalism (critiqued: worth by birth and class).

101521.heading: The Faraway Paladin
101521.label: From summaries
101521.life_message: A life is not wasted when it is given in faithful, loving service to others; the real death is a stagnant life lived only for oneself.

content.framing: Endorsed (defense of the weak); mercy shown

delivery.evidence: ANN's light-novel reviewer finds the theme carried by the family bond and a warning against a self-centered, stagnant life rather than by sermons; Will reflects often on his past life (ANN notes he does so too often).
delivery.note: The message is voiced through Will's reflections on his wasted past life and his vows, but shown mainly through what he does for others.

personified.ideology: Faithful service instead of a wasted life
Undead parents teaching how to live; Gus vows to live as he chooses
An unchanging world; undeath instead of rebirth
Distrust born of rejection, turned to loyalty

101521.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism (found family and rebuilt towns), Pagan/occult (a real pantheon), with a Christian-like devotional seriousness.

154008.heading: The Fed-Up Office Lady Wants to Serve the Villainess
154008.label: From summaries
154008.life_message: Devoted, capable service to someone you believe in can give a discarded worker purpose, and looking past someone's "villain" role can change her fate.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: A comedy-romance in which the themes of work and devotion are carried by plot and jokes; Okazu notes Natori is clueless about the romance for a while (vol. 2).
delivery.note: Themes of work and devotion come through comedy rather than argument; the age gap is not, in sources opened, discussed by the story itself (to verify).

154008.dominant: Pragmatism, Progressivism (girls' love as natural), Expressive individualism.

54705.heading: The Flowers of Evil
54705.label: From summaries
54705.life_message: Growing up means facing the darkness in yourself honestly instead of worshiping an ideal or trying to escape through destruction; an ordinary life shared with real people is the "other side" worth reaching.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.frequency: Pervasive in the first arc, rare in the second
content.framing: Shown with consequences; the assault condemned

delivery.evidence: Wrong Every Time says the work understands its characters rather than judging them, while separating their desires from their harmful acts; reviews describe mood and imagery, not lectures.
delivery.note: The message is carried by consequences, mood and the second arc's recovery rather than stated; Nakamura's worldview gets a full and sympathetic hearing before the story moves past it.

personified.ideology: Literary idealism and the wish to be special
Nihilistic contempt and escape from normal life
The perfect girl who wants to be seen as she is

54705.dominant: Existentialism (the search for an authentic self), Nihilism (voiced, then moved past), Expressive individualism, Secular humanism (recovery through people and art).

140475.heading: The Fragrant Flower Blooms With Dignity (Saka Mikami)
140475.label: From summaries
140475.life_message: A good life comes from seeing people as they are rather than as their label, from honest and patient kindness, and from working through fear and division together; love grows slowly and is tended.

delivery.evidence: CSM: "An important theme is how stereotypes are harmful." The prejudiced side (Saku, Subaru, Ms. Toki) is given understandable reasons, and Ms. Toki's past injury explains her stance (vols. 23-24).
delivery.note: The anti-prejudice theme is stated often in dialogue, but it is carried by small scenes of kindness rather than speeches, and no character is a cartoon villain.

personified.ideology: Do not judge by appearance; gentle masculinity
Distrust of the privileged other school

140475.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Secular humanism.

31023.heading: The Ghost in the Shell
31023.label: From summaries
31023.life_message: Who you are lies in the mind and its power to grow, not in the body you happen to have; to stay alive, any kind of life, human or machine, must risk changing and joining with something new.

content.framing: Neutral (police action); torture and murder by criminals condemned

delivery.evidence: Shirow's footnotes argue his views directly (death penalty, channeling, technology; Wikipedia), and the Puppeteer states its case for being alive; Batou and Aramaki voice doubts.
delivery.note: Ideas are argued openly in dialogue and in dense footnotes, though the casework keeps them from feeling like lectures; ANN advises skipping the notes on a first read.

personified.ideology: Identity as mind; openness to transformation
A new life form seeking to evolve
Secret state power over minds and machines

31023.dominant: Transhumanism, Existentialism (what is the self?), Naturalism (consciousness from information).

105641.heading: The Girl I Like Forgot Her Glasses
105641.label: From summaries
105641.life_message: Small, patient acts of kindness are how first love begins and grows: seeing someone clearly is about attention and care, not eyesight.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe short, episodic chapters with a few jokes and a slowly growing crush (ANN; Final Weapon); no message is stated.
delivery.note: Values show only through small acts of kindness; there is no argument to make and no opposing view.

105641.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (patient kindness), Communitarianism (classmates and families).

125280.heading: The Girl I Saved on the Train Turned Out to Be My Childhood Friend
125280.label: From summaries
125280.life_message: Quiet courage and honest feelings matter more than popularity; real closeness is rebuilt by facing the past and saying what you feel.

delivery.evidence: Values come through Ryou's actions and the girls' choices; reviewers describe a low-stress romantic comedy with no lecturing (ANN; Anime UK News).
delivery.note: There is no worldview conflict to argue; the only wrongdoer is the groper in ch. 1.

personified.ideology: Do the right thing quietly; doubt your own worth
Go after what you want, in love and in work

125280.dominant: Expressive individualism (following your dream), Classical virtue ethics (courage, honesty), Communitarianism (friends and class).

103184.heading: The Girl with the Sanpaku Eyes
103184.label: From summaries
103184.life_message: A gentle heart matters more than a fierce first impression, and small, brave, honest steps toward another person, with friends cheering you on, can turn shyness into love.

delivery.evidence: No villains or rivals; the point about appearances is carried by the premise and Katou's behavior (ANN; MyAnimeList user reviews).
delivery.note: The story never states a lesson; it shows small acts of courage and kindness.

personified.ideology: Gentle heart behind a fierce face; courage to speak

103184.dominant: Communitarianism (a supportive class) and Expressive individualism (finding the courage to say how you feel).

80217.heading: the gods lie.
80217.label: From summaries
80217.life_message: Children need adults who keep their promises; loyalty to a friend is precious, but some secrets are too heavy for a child to carry alone.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: ANN praises its skillful understatement and expression through body language; Solrad finds the message about support systems in the events, not in speeches.
delivery.note: The message is carried by events and silences; adults are shown as flawed without lectures.

personified.ideology: Loyalty to a friend over rules
Keeping the family together at any cost

80217.dominant: Communitarianism (the need for support systems), Duty ethics (promises kept and broken), Classical virtue ethics (loyalty and courage)

100207.heading: The Great Jahy Will Not Be Defeated!
100207.label: From summaries
100207.life_message: Losing your power is not the end: by working honestly, accepting help and learning humility, Jahy builds a good life out of nothing, and the friends she makes become as precious as the throne she lost.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe gag-driven comedy with a warm core, not lessons (Anime UK News; ANN This Week in Anime); Jahy's rivals are played for comedy, not condemned.
delivery.note: The humility-and-work message comes through Jahy's small improvements, not speeches.

personified.ideology: Generous care for a struggling worker

100207.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (humility and perseverance), Communitarianism (neighbors as family), Stoicism (refusing to be beaten).

108441.heading: The Greatest Demon Lord Is Reborn as a Typical Nobody
108441.label: From summaries
108441.life_message: Power without friends is a lonely prison; real friendship means being accepted for who you are and protecting the people who accepted you.

content.framing: Neutral (fantasy combat; the hero always wins)
Played for comedy (harem); the threatened assault is condemned

delivery.evidence: Ard states his wish for friends from the first chapter (AniList blurb); villains such as Elzard and Disaster-Rogue are given lonely motives that Ard names (anime ep. 5, 12).
delivery.note: The friendship message is stated openly and repeated; the comedy and fights carry it.

personified.ideology: Hatred of the world from loneliness

108441.dominant: Communitarianism (friendship), Might makes right (power fantasy), Expressive individualism, Pagan/occult (as fantasy setting).

154222.heading: The Hero and the Sage, Reincarnated and Engaged
154222.label: From summaries
154222.life_message: Old enemies who respected each other can become partners; strength is best used to protect others, and love grows from knowing someone fully.

content.framing: Mixed: heroic combat endorsed; killing innocents condemned

delivery.evidence: Gaffney: most characters are good or follow a bad leader under threat; jerks become comedy relief; "not really big on moral greyness."
delivery.note: A comedy-romance with action; values are shown through the couple's choices, and opponents are rarely given a real case.

154222.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (loyalty and courage), Might makes right (an overpowered couple, explored), Pagan/occult (a world of magic and rebirth). Rebirth is a plot device here, not a Hindu or Buddhist teaching, so those lenses score below 3.

101238.heading: The Hero Laughs While Walking the Path of Vengeance a Second Time
101238.label: From summaries
101238.life_message: Betrayal earns the betrayer unlimited suffering, and only someone bound to you cannot betray you; the story invites the reader to enjoy the revenge.

content.framing: Endorsed (revenge and torture are the hero's path and the story's pleasure)

delivery.evidence: Reviewers find no moral argument, only revenge and torture; the case against revenge is not voiced in volume 1 (ANN; Anime UK News on the light novel).
delivery.note: The message is carried by what the story lingers on and rewards (the hero's laughter, the victims' suffering), not by speeches. The betrayers get almost no development in volume 1 (ANN).

personified.ideology: Revenge as justice; trust no one
Shared hatred; devotion to her master

101238.dominant: Might makes right, Nihilism, Hedonism (in cruelty), distrust of every authority.

81233.heading: The Heroic Legend of Arslan
81233.label: From summaries
81233.life_message: A ruler earns loyalty through compassion, listening and justice for the powerless rather than through birth or force, and freedom for slaves and for conscience is worth fighting for, though it costs dearly.

delivery.evidence: WWAC says the story takes on slavery's practical problems directly; ANN's Martin says it invites discussion of religion and raises substantial questions about slavery; Bodin is drawn as a fanatical blowhard (ANN).
delivery.note: Big ideas (slavery, religious war, the duties of a king) are carried by rulers and factions and argued openly; Pars's own faults are shown beside Lusitania's, though the zealot leaders are one-sided.

personified.ideology: religious zealotry: kill the unbeliever, burn the books

81233.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (just kingship), Progressivism (abolition), Patriotism (defensive), critique of theocracy and rule by force.

103850.heading: The Hidden Dungeon Only I Can Enter
103850.label: From summaries
103850.life_message: A poor young man can rise by cleverness, effort and kindness, using his power to save others; the series also presents pleasure, especially romantic and sexual excitement, as the healthy fuel of strength.

content.framing: Endorsed as comedy and as a power source
Mixed: peeping condemned; sexual touching by a teacher and harem behavior played as rewards

delivery.evidence: Snobbish nobles and peepers are cartoon foils (anime ep. 1, 9-10); Maria states the merit-over-rank view outright in the manga (Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: Merit over privilege is stated by sympathetic characters; the pleasure-as-power idea is built into the game rules rather than argued.

personified.ideology: Merit, kindness and pleasure as fuel

103850.dominant: Hedonism (pleasure as power), Classical virtue ethics (kindness and courage), Pragmatism (editing skills), Critical theory (merit versus inherited rank).

135981.heading: The Hunters Guild: Red Hood
135981.label: From summaries
135981.life_message: Protect people who cannot protect themselves, work together instead of tearing each other down, and refuse to live out a part that someone else has written for you.

content.framing: Neutral (monster-hunting action); the werewolves' killing condemned

delivery.evidence: The final arc states its theme through info-dumps and meta commentary (AniList and MyAnimeList user reviews); the villain-author is given a motive, but the cut-short run leaves little room to argue it.
delivery.note: The first two arcs carry the message in action; the last chapters say it outright.

personified.ideology: Freedom to write your own story; protect others
Control of others through a written script

135981.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (courage, protection), Existentialism (choose your own story), Postmodernism (metafiction).

109728.heading: The Ice Guy and the Cool Girl
109728.label: From summaries
109728.life_message: Being accepted for your quirks by kind, patient people makes ordinary life warm, and love grows from small acts of care.

delivery.evidence: No speeches; acceptance and kindness are shown in small episodes (Comics Beat; ANN preview).
delivery.note: The message is carried by gestures (tea, gifts, nursing a fever) rather than stated.

personified.ideology: Feelings cannot stay hidden; learn to speak up

109728.dominant: Communitarianism (the office as a kind community, affirmed), Classical virtue ethics (kindness and patience), Traditionalism (shrines, family and seasons, explored).

123093.heading: The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World
123093.label: From summaries
123093.life_message: Real strength is protecting your friends and growing through honest effort, not birth or rank; even someone scarred by war can learn to live, laugh and belong.

delivery.evidence: The snobbish nobles are exaggerated (Rebecca Silverman, ANN preview); Albert gets a real change of heart (ep. 5). The war's cost is stated by Lydia (Kodansha vol. 13).
delivery.note: Themes arrive through duels and rescues rather than speeches; Ray states his values plainly when friends need encouragement.

personified.ideology: Humble strength in service of friends

123093.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Traditionalism (aristocracy critiqued), Transhumanism (critiqued), Patriotism / nationalism (explored).

156656.heading: The Ichinose Family's Deadly Sins
156656.label: From summaries
156656.life_message: No family is perfect; running from what you did into a comfortable dream only deepens the harm, and a family can go on only by facing its past, together and still quarrelling.

delivery.evidence: The message comes through mystery reveals and confessions (Real Sound via Japanese Wikipedia: the hero does not fix things with a special power); Sota states the need to accept the past.
delivery.note: Each family member's room and memory reveal his or her "sin"; the reader judges alongside an unreliable narrator.

personified.ideology: Leaving to make a chosen family

98347.heading: The Ideal Sponger Life
98347.label: From summaries
98347.life_message: A marriage begun as a bargain can become real love and partnership when each spouse supports the other's work, and a man finds purpose in protecting his family rather than in doing nothing.

content.framing: Neutral (sex within marriage treated positively; concubinage accepted)

delivery.evidence: Manga Bookshelf presents it as worldbuilding and politics without moralizing; ANN praises its careful handling of the premise; rival nobles are capable schemers rather than fools.
delivery.note: The story argues through outcomes (a loving marriage, safe children, good trade deals) rather than speeches.

personified.ideology: a woman ruler keeping power in a patriarchal court

personified.character: General Pujol and rival marriage candidates

98347.dominant: Pragmatism (problems solved by competence and bargaining), Traditionalism (marriage, lineage and monarchy), Feminism (a queen keeping power), Hedonism (the idle-life premise, outgrown).

127224.heading: The Impregnable Demon King's Castle and the Expelled Black Mage of the Hero's Party
127224.label: From summaries
127224.life_message: Skills that others dismiss can be exactly what someone else needs; find the people who value you, and stay loyal to the friends who stood up for you.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: Chapter titles such as "We Will Live in the World We Chose" (ch. 42) and "To the Hero I Admired From That Day" (ch. 20-22) suggest the theme is stated at arc climaxes (title only); the old party is shown as mistaken, not wicked (TV Tropes).
delivery.note: A light workplace fantasy with an implied message about valuing overlooked skills and keeping old friendships.

127224.dominant: Communitarianism (found workplace family), Pragmatism, Expressive individualism (the underrated finding his place).

123089.heading: The Inferior Magic Swordsman
123089.label: From summaries
123089.life_message: A person his society writes off can rise through patient, well-planned effort, and the strength he earns is best used to protect his companions.

content.framing: Neutral (played as harem comedy and romance)

delivery.evidence: Readers describe a light, generic progression story with no stated thesis; the anti-discrimination point is carried by results, not speeches.
delivery.note: Any message about prejudice is carried by the underdog's rise rather than stated, as far as summaries show.

personified.ideology: Rank by level; contempt for outsiders
Religion as a tool of power

144599.heading: THE ISEKAI DOCTOR: Any sufficiently advanced medical science is indistinguishable from magic.
144599.label: From summaries
144599.life_message: Medicine is for everyone, friend or enemy, of any race or rank; patient knowledge and compassion heal where privilege and superstition leave people to suffer.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: Each case teaches real medicine (MangaUpdates and AniList tag it Educational); the hospital-for-all ideal is stated (v4 blurb). The human side has a would-be reformer in its archbishop (v6), so it is not wholly a strawman, though its hierarchy is shown resisting.
delivery.note: Message carried by cases: each patient is an argument that knowledge beats curses and privilege.

personified.ideology: Freedom and learning for the oppressed

144599.dominant: Secular humanism (medicine and compassion), Pragmatism, Duty ethics (treat every patient); Communitarianism (a hospital for all) and a critique of monopoly and domination.

109111.heading: The Isekai Returnee Is Too OP for the Modern World
109111.label: From summaries
109111.life_message: Overwhelming strength is meant to protect the weak and stop the cruel; a bullied boy can become the hero others need, even if it costs him a quiet life.

content.framing: Endorsed (the hero's beatdowns of villains and monsters)

delivery.evidence: No source describes a stated message; villains, from the blurbs, exist to be beaten.
delivery.note: A light power fantasy with little argument; the "hero protects the weak" ideal appears in vol. 4.

109111.dominant: Strength rules, Pagan/occult (Japanese folk spirits), Hedonism (fan service).

56769.heading: The Kawai Complex Guide to Manors and Hostel Behavior
56769.label: From summaries
56769.life_message: Living alongside odd, imperfect people teaches patience and care, and love grows slowly through everyday kindness and honest words.

content.framing: Sexual jokes played for laughs; the main romance chaste and respectful
Played for comedy, with a sad edge

delivery.evidence: The message comes through everyday scenes and running gags; no character argues a worldview, and the eccentric adults are neither condemned nor reformed.
delivery.note: A sitcom structure (set up a sweet moment, then derail it, in Paul Jensen's description) keeps the message light.

personified.ideology: Introversion; reluctance to rely on others

56769.dominant: Communitarianism (found family in a shared house), Classical virtue ethics (patience), Expressive individualism (accepting quirks).

112203.heading: The Kingdoms of Ruin
112203.label: From summaries
112203.life_message: Persecution breeds hatred, and hatred can consume a person and a world; love, loyalty and companionship can slowly turn a heart away from revenge, though the story lets the wronged fight back.

content.framing: Mixed: the witch hunt condemned; the hero's massacre presented as understandable but questioned
Mostly condemned (abuse, trafficking); some exploitative imagery

delivery.evidence: Doroka and Punch argue against revenge and are heard, not mocked; the empire's case for extermination is drawn as cruel and hypocritical.
delivery.note: The story states its themes in Doroka's pleas and Adonis's monologues, but carries them through battles more than speeches.

personified.ideology: Revenge on humanity for a loved one's death
Science supremacy; extermination of the obsolete
Love as control; any cost for a lost love

112203.dominant: Pagan/occult, Might makes right (critiqued), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Nihilism (explored).

108768.heading: The Klutzy Class Monitor and the Girl with the Short Skirt
108768.label: From summaries
108768.life_message: Look past someone's surface: honesty and kindness under a stiff or flashy exterior are what make friendship and love grow.

delivery.evidence: The point (look past appearances) is carried by gags and character reveals, not speeches; the rule-keeper and the rule-bender are both sympathetic.
delivery.note: A light gag romance; the message is in the pairing itself.

108768.dominant: Expressive individualism (be yourself), Communitarianism (friends and families), Duty ethics (sincere rule-keeping).

33575.heading: The Legend of the Strongest, Kurosawa!
33575.label: From summaries
33575.life_message: An overlooked, middle-aged nobody can still live with dignity by refusing to bow to cruelty and by standing up for people weaker than himself; a life is measured by its heart, not its status.

content.framing: Mixed: bullies and attackers condemned; Kurosawa's fighting framed as admirable
Shown with consequences; met with compassion

delivery.evidence: Kurosawa's inner monologue and speeches state the theme often (Honcierge stresses lines about living for something beyond survival); villains such as Miki are drawn without nuance, while delinquents like Nakane are redeemed.
delivery.note: The message is carried by comic misadventure and long interior monologue in Fukumoto's style rather than lectures, but Kurosawa does make speeches.

personified.ideology: Wealth and cruelty toward the poor

33575.dominant: Existentialism, Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Bushido / honor code.

85952.heading: The Legendary Hero Is Dead!
85952.label: From summaries
85952.life_message: Even a selfish, unlikely person can become a real hero by taking up a burden others left behind and protecting the people he loves.

content.framing: Mixed: battle action endorsed; villains' cruelty condemned

delivery.evidence: Parody comedy carries the message; darker themes surface through reveals (Sion's suicide, the king's nature) (fan wiki; Wikipedia).
delivery.note: Necromancers who hate humans are given a history of persecution, so even villains get reasons.

85952.dominant: Pagan/occult (necromancy as the heroes' tool), Hedonism (lechery comedy), Classical virtue ethics (growth in courage), Might makes right (critiqued).

99602.heading: The Magic in this Other World is Too Far Behind! (manga)
99602.label: From summaries
99602.life_message: No one has the right to draft you into their war; keep the promises you made to your family, and use your gifts to protect the friends you choose.

content.framing: Neutral (harem comedy); curse content unconfirmed in the manga

delivery.evidence: ANN's review of the light novels says Suimei angrily tells the king the summoning was wrong and that the reviewer finds him right, not preachy; Reiji's choice to help is not mocked.
delivery.note: The hero states his objection outright in the opening; later volumes carry the theme through action rather than argument.

personified.ideology: using outsiders to solve a war

99602.dominant: Pagan/occult (Western esoteric magic as the hero's craft), Liberalism (consent: summoning as kidnapping), Libertarianism (refusing conscription), Duty ethics (a promise to his father).

122344.heading: The Magical Revolution of the Reincarnated Princess and the Genius Young Lady
122344.label: From summaries
122344.life_message: Your worth does not depend on the gift or role others assign you; shared burdens, honest love and useful invention can open a closed, unfair order to everyone.

content.framing: Mixed: monster and dragon combat endorsed; Algard's attack condemned
Endorsed (the central romance); fan service criticized by reviewers

delivery.evidence: Algard is given real reasons (he hated the kingdom for rejecting his sister; Wikipedia) and the parents are shown as caring though constrained; Count Chartreuse and the elitist nobles are flatter. Reform is stated openly at the end (ep. 12).
delivery.note: The case against magical elitism is made through Anis's results and Algard's confession; the romance is shown rather than argued.

personified.ideology: Worth through knowledge and invention, not birth
Finding one's own purpose; love that takes up another's burden
Purge a corrupt elite by seizing absolute power

122344.dominant: Progressivism, Expressive individualism, Traditionalism (critiqued), Liberalism (equal standing regardless of birth).

114917.heading: The Maid I Hired Recently Is Mysterious
114917.label: From summaries
114917.life_message: Love and loyal care can rebuild a family after loss, and honest, simple words disarm teasing; the story treats a young boy's love for his older maid as sweet.

content.framing: Romance between a boy and his older caregiver treated as sweet; teasing played for comedy

delivery.evidence: A gag-driven comedy; the one dissenting view (Natsume's, that Yuuri is unworthy) is given a hearing and then softened (eps. 9-11).
delivery.note: The story never argues for its romance; it assumes it, which is why some reviewers object.

personified.ideology: Devoted service as repayment of gratitude
Status and wealth define a worthy master

114917.dominant: Found family after loss; gratitude and service; a child's first love played for comedy.

106601.heading: The Misfit of Demon King Academy
106601.label: From summaries
106601.life_message: Worth is not set by bloodline or rank; real strength is shown by protecting friends and family and by making peace, and no "fate" has the right to take away the people you love.

content.framing: Mixed: the hero's cruelty to bullies played as cool; killings by villains condemned

delivery.evidence: ANN: prejudice works as world-building and comes through Anos's thoughts; the highbloods and the teacher are drawn as sneering bullies with no real case (ch. 2, 3, 13).
delivery.note: The anti-prejudice message is carried by plot and Anos's inner monologue rather than speeches; the blood-supremacist side is never given a fair hearing in the manga.

personified.ideology: Worth beyond bloodline, backed by overwhelming power
Honor of the pure royal line above kin
Pride of lineage (a mask for love)

106601.dominant: Strength rules (explored: power that protects versus power that rules by birth), Liberalism (equal standing regardless of blood), Communitarianism (family and loyal friends).

136109.heading: The Moon on a Rainy Night
136109.label: From summaries
136109.life_message: Real closeness comes from seeing another person as they are and making room for them on their own terms, not pitying them; love grows out of that kind of patient friendship.

delivery.evidence: Friedman calls it a bit of an explainer manga that lets Kanon correct Saki's mistakes (Okazu), but Farris (ANN, via Wikipedia) praises how much it says with little; antagonists like Ayano and Tomita get their side told.
delivery.note: The message is carried by characters' choices with some gentle explaining about hearing loss; no one is a strawman.

personified.ideology: independence over pity or special treatment
empathy that respects the other's terms

136109.dominant: Progressivism (disability dignity and LGBTQ inclusion), Communitarianism, Expressive individualism.

177096.heading: The Mortifying Ordeal of Being Seen
177096.label: From summaries
177096.life_message: Admitting what you feel, desire included, and letting someone see you is frightening but worth it; open, mutual attraction can be the start of real love.

delivery.evidence: Gag-comedy chapters carry the premise; no character argues for restraint in any source opened (VIZ synopses; ANN).
delivery.note: The message is the premise itself: open, mutual desire is good fun, and the "ordeal" of being seen is worth it.

177096.dominant: Hedonism (desire as play), Expressive individualism (say what you feel), with a role-reversed gaze.

123463.heading: The Most Notorious "Talker" Runs the World's Greatest Clan
123463.label: From summaries
123463.life_message: In a harsh world, the weakest can rise to the top through will, cunning and ruthlessness; the story admires the winner and asks little about the cost to the people he uses.

content.framing: Mixed: battles as action; mafia cruelty condemned; the hero's own cruelty presented as clever

delivery.evidence: Walter objects and leaves (likely ch. 4-6) and Leon's idealism gets a hearing, but the plot proves Noel right each time (Wikipedia anime summaries; ANN).
delivery.note: Noel states his creed openly, and the publisher's blurb says good and evil are all the same to him; the story sells it through victories rather than argument.

personified.ideology: Results by any means; strength of will

123463.dominant: Pragmatism (ends justify means), Strength rules (affirmed), Expressive individualism (ambition), Utilitarianism (the Valiant threat).

31766.heading: The Music of Marie
31766.label: From summaries
31766.life_message: A peace built on faith and on giving up the hunger to own and to advance is precious and fragile, and keeping it can cost a person everything; the last twist asks whether that faith is a gift or a wound.

content.framing: Condemned (the horror of a world without peace)
Mixed: young love and marriage customs shown warmly; Kai's fixation shown as unsettling

delivery.evidence: Scripture-style passages run through the book (Anime UK News); Farris (ANN) calls the plot beats sledgehammer-like, while The Outerhaven and AnimeNation read it as a parable that lets readers weigh the choice; the twist complicates the faith message (Farris).
delivery.note: The book states its premise about desire, technology and war openly, then complicates it with a tragic second half and an epilogue twist; only one reviewer calls it heavy-handed.

personified.ideology: Truth and devotion at any cost
Ordinary love and the wish to fly

31766.dominant: Buddhist ideas (craving as the root of strife), Traditionalism (suspicion of progress), Authoritarianism (benevolent control, explored), Christian imagery.

85978.heading: The New Gate
85978.label: From summaries
85978.life_message: Great strength is for protecting the weak, and a person can find a true home and lasting bonds in a world he once treated as a game.

content.framing: Mixed: fan service as decoration; romance chaste

delivery.evidence: The protective ethic is carried by rescues and loyalty rather than speeches; villains (kidnappers, demons) are flat, while the duel with Girard gives his warrior's view full respect.
delivery.note: The message that power should serve the weak is shown through Shin's choices, not argued.

personified.ideology: Warrior's honor and a chosen death

personified.character: Millie's captors in the Church at Shigerus

85978.dominant: Communitarianism, Classical virtue ethics, Bushido / honor code (strength used to protect; loyalty to old companions).

122123.heading: The NPCs in this Village Sim Game Must Be Real!
122123.label: From summaries
122123.life_message: Taking responsibility for others, even small, imperfect steps for people who depend on you, can draw a withdrawn person back into life, work and family.

delivery.evidence: Recovery is shown through Yoshio's choices and family scenes (Seven Seas blurbs; MyAnimeList reviews); villains are simple threats.
delivery.note: The message about responsibility is clear but carried by the plot rather than speeches.

122123.dominant: Communitarianism (protecting the village and family), Secular humanism (recovery through human effort), Transhumanism (are AI people real?).

106029.heading: The One. Later On...
106029.label: From summaries
106029.life_message: Heartbreak need not define you: an ordinary person who keeps going can become strong, and strength is best used to protect people who are trapped or controlled by others.

content.framing: Mixed: fan service played as comedy; coercion condemned

106029.dominant: Might makes right (strength used to protect), Hedonism (harem comedy and fan service), Classical virtue ethics (a decent hero).

delivery.evidence: Sources describe plot and comedy only (The Slings & Arrows; PRH; BOOK☆WALKER); no reviewer calls it preachy or finds an argued worldview.
delivery.note: The values come through who Wazu protects and who gets exposed, not through speeches.

30049.heading: The Prince of Tennis
30049.label: From summaries
30049.life_message: Talent must be matched by hard work and loyalty to the team, and the deepest reason to play is not winning or living up to your father but the joy of the game itself.

content.framing: Mixed: deliberate injury play condemned or shown as a flaw; playing on through injury often admired
Mixed: playing through injury admired; cockiness and ball attacks shown as flaws

delivery.evidence: Values emerge from matches and training; rival schools get backstories (Fudomine's abused freshmen, Akutsu's reasons, Yukimura's illness). ANN found the first volume thin on theme; the clearest stated lesson is Tezuka telling Ryoma to find his own tennis (v5-6).
delivery.note: A tournament story whose message is carried by matches, not lectures; rivals are usually respected opponents.

personified.ideology: Confidence that grows into joy in the game
Duty and self-sacrifice for the team
Absolute victory as a team code

30049.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (excellence through training), Communitarianism (the team as pillar), Expressive individualism (finding your own style).

87423.heading: The Promised Neverland
87423.label: From summaries
87423.life_message: A good life means refusing to accept a system that treats people as food, refusing to leave anyone behind, and refusing to answer cruelty with extermination: Emma wants everyone to live, enemies included, and she pays for it herself.

delivery.evidence: Common Sense Media says it sides with the children and condemns the social system; Shirai says there is no specific message and leaves interpretation to readers (VIZ interview); Sequential Tart praised how both sides of the Emma-Norman debate are argued (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The three leads embody competing ethics of survival, and the plot tests each choice.

personified.ideology: Protect your own by removing the threat
Save the few who can make it
Humans as stock for an elite

87423.dominant: Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Duty ethics (affirmed), Utilitarianism (critiqued), Secular humanism, Communitarianism.

100230.heading: The Quintessential Quintuplets
100230.label: From summaries
100230.life_message: A good life is built by honest effort, loyalty to family and the willingness to grow; love means choosing one person for life while keeping faith with everyone else you love.

content.framing: Endorsed (romance ending in marriage); Neutral (fan-service gags); kisses without asking treated as romantic

delivery.evidence: Lessons on effort, family and fidelity come through exam arcs and sister conflicts; wrongdoers (Ichika) are given reasons and a path back. Reviewers opened treat it as solid genre romance, not as preaching.
delivery.note: The harem framing itself goes unexamined, but the ending rejects the harem fantasy in favor of one marriage.

100230.dominant: Confucian ethics, Classical virtue ethics, Traditionalism, Communitarianism.

166742.heading: The Ramparts of Ice
166742.label: From summaries
166742.life_message: Walls built to avoid being hurt also keep out friendship and love; honest words, patience and friends who accept you as you are can melt them, and caring for others must not mean hiding your own feelings.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Neutral; insincere dating shown as harmful
Shown with consequences; healing through friendship

delivery.evidence: Lessons emerge through character arcs and frank conversations; flawed characters (Minato, Miki, Tsubasa, Momoka) are given reasons and room to change (Wikipedia; ANN, episode 11).
delivery.note: Inner monologue states feelings plainly, but the story rarely lectures; even the antagonist Momoka gets a reckoning and a resolution.

personified.ideology: Protecting yourself by keeping others out
Fixing others while hiding your own feelings
Love goes to whoever moves first; manipulation

166742.dominant: Communitarianism (friends as the cure for isolation), Expressive individualism (be your real self), Classical virtue ethics (honesty, courage, patience).

107611.heading: The Reformation of the World as Overseen by a Realist Demon King
107611.label: From summaries
107611.life_message: A ruler who thinks clearly, plans ahead and treats his people fairly can win and build a better realm, even if he uses deception and hard tactics against his enemies.

content.framing: Endorsed as strategy (wars of conquest won by the hero)

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Neutral (fan service); context of attempted-assault tags unknown

delivery.evidence: Astaroth explains his reasoning to his subordinates (MangaUpdates blurb dialogue); Siliconera says his choices are brilliant but not moral; ANN says the book frames him "in a kind of lawful evil light" with a kind heart beneath.
delivery.note: The realist method is stated outright and always works; rivals who rule badly are drawn as foils rather than argued with.

personified.ideology: realism: results over rules, with fair rule at home

97925.heading: The Reincarnated Evil Dragon
97925.label: From summaries
97925.life_message: Power is best used gently, to protect the weak and the people you have come to love, and whoever preys on the weak, monster, man or god, will answer for it.

content.framing: Endorsed as justice for the weak; villains' cruelty condemned

delivery.evidence: The villains (minions who slaughter slimes, a murder ring, arrogant gods) are wholly evil in every source; Ja's own choices, such as buying Irene, are not questioned in any summary.
delivery.note: Little stated message beyond protecting companions; the tagline frames Ja as soft-hearted rather than as a model of a philosophy.

personified.ideology: Live freely and protect your own
The gods' right to rule humans

97925.dominant: Might makes right (explored), Pagan/occult settings with gods as villains, Hedonism; a protector's revenge.

123544.heading: The Reincarnation of the Strongest Exorcist in Another World
123544.label: From summaries
123544.life_message: Power is safest with someone who has learned from betrayal: protect the few you love, trust carefully, and refuse to let rulers or merchants use people as tools.

content.framing: Endorsed as the hero's power; cruelty by villains condemned

delivery.evidence: Seika's cautious philosophy is shown through his choices and inner calculations; villains such as the Merchants' Association and the demon team are flat, while Fiona and the principal are shown as clever rather than evil (Wikipedia, eps. 7, 13).
delivery.note: A light isekai adventure; the message is in the hero's choices, not speeches.

personified.ideology: Prudent, hidden power used for loved ones

123544.dominant: Pagan/occult (onmyōdō magic and spirit servants, affirmed), Pragmatism (cunning caution), Might makes right (explored: overwhelming power used for friends).

157751.heading: The Revenge of My Youth: Re Life with an Angelic Girl
157751.label: From summaries
157751.life_message: A second chance is best spent becoming someone others can lean on: speak up, work hard for the people around you, protect the person you love from cruelty, and treasure your family while you have them.

content.framing: Condemned (the bullying and overwork that cause it)

delivery.evidence: ANN and The Outerhaven describe familiar, trope-driven plotting; the boss and bully are flat villains, while the message is carried by the hero's choices.
delivery.note: Its redo-your-life message is shown in action and in the hero's inner monologue rather than in lectures.

personified.ideology: Turn regret into courage and service

157751.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (courage and diligence), Pragmatism (adult skills at school), Critical theory (exploitative work, labor critique).

30660.heading: The Rose of Versailles
30660.label: From summaries
30660.life_message: Conscience and love can lead a person to break with rank, family and privilege to stand with the suffering, even at the cost of her life; a life lived truly, however short, is not wasted.

content.frequency: Occasional, heavy in the revolution chapters
content.framing: Shown with consequences; the people's revolt is presented with sympathy
Mixed: love across rank honored; adultery shown as tragic love; coercion condemned

delivery.evidence: Ikeda's politics (class consciousness, women's rights) shape the arc (Wikipedia, citing McKnight and Anan), but the royals, the general and even the queen are drawn with sympathy, and the revolution's cruelty to the royal children is shown (Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The message is carried by Oscar's change of heart and by melodrama rather than speeches, though Oscar and Bernard voice the people's case directly.

personified.ideology: Conscience, equality and freedom for the people and for women
Royal privilege, charm and personal feeling
Loyalty to the crown and tradition
Court ambition and use of others

30660.dominant: Feminism, Marxism (class struggle), Liberalism (rights and popular sovereignty), Progressivism.

97216.heading: The Saga of Tanya the Evil
97216.label: From summaries
97216.life_message: Cold, self-serving reason turns a person into a monster and still cannot save them: every clever plan Tanya makes to escape the war pulls her deeper in, while a god who demands worship comes off no better than the atheist he punishes.

content.framing: Mixed: aerial combat played as thrilling; atrocity and war's cost shown with consequences and condemned in the historians' reports

delivery.evidence: The critique comes through irony (Tanya's inner monologue versus how others misread her as heroic, Fandom Post vol. 2) and the historians' reports (ch. 9, 40); Being X is a caricature, while Rerugen and the generals are drawn fairly.
delivery.note: Black comedy and military detail carry the message; there are no lectures, but the title calls the hero "the evil."

97216.dominant: Utilitarianism (Critiqued), Christian (Critiqued: a petty god), Patriotism / nationalism and Collectivism/authoritarianism (Explored), Might makes right (Explored).

101503.heading: The Saint's Magic Power is Omnipotent
101503.label: From summaries
101503.life_message: Quiet, diligent work done to help others matters more than titles or looks, and love in many forms is what brings out healing power.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: Values come through Sei's work and choices; the prince's error is played as a misunderstanding he must live with rather than as villainy (Wikipedia), but scheming nobles are thin.
delivery.note: A cozy, low-conflict story: the message is carried by what Sei does, not by speeches.

101503.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (diligence and humble service), Pragmatism (research), Communitarianism (the Institute and the knights); a light Feminism (the overlooked capable woman).

110062.heading: The Savior’s Book Cafe Story in Another World
110062.label: From summaries
110062.life_message: A modest life of books, hospitality and honest work is a worthy choice, and a person with power still steps up to protect others when it truly matters.

content.framing: Condemned (the cruel savior's abuse); neutral (monster attack)

delivery.evidence: Tsukina's choice is shown through her life at the café; the opposite view (power as privilege) is carried by a cartoonishly cruel savior (ANN).
delivery.note: The quiet-life message is carried by mood and situation, not argument; a MyAnimeList reviewer calls the protagonist too perfect and the monarchy overly kind.

personified.ideology: A quiet, self-chosen life of books and hospitality

110062.dominant: Expressive individualism (a self-chosen quiet life), Communitarianism, Traditionalism (courtship and marriage), Classical virtue ethics.

129117.heading: The Seven Deadly Sins: Four Knights of the Apocalypse
129117.label: From summaries
129117.life_message: Hope is something friends make together: people who trust one another can face even a world that has decided they are its destroyers, and no promise of a perfect world justifies wiping out those who are different.

content.framing: Neutral (fantasy action); cruelty and purges condemned
Mixed: fan service unjudged; romance endorsed

delivery.evidence: Arthur's utopia and Ironside's "greater good" are given motives; Ardbeg's grief is sympathetic and he turns back (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: Friendship and hope are shown in action and named in Percival's power rather than preached.

personified.ideology: A perfect world for humans only
The greater good by any means

129117.dominant: Communitarianism (friendship as power), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued), Might makes right (critiqued), Pagan/occult (fantasy myth).

144374.heading: The Shiunji Family Children (Shiunji-ke no Kodomotachi)
144374.label: From summaries
144374.life_message: Family is made by shared years and loyalty rather than blood, though the story keeps that bond in tension with romance by letting the sisters fall for their brother and hinting that he will marry one of them.

content.framing: Mixed: Arata refuses every advance, while the framing plays the tension for romance and fan service

delivery.evidence: Ouka declares incest disgusting (anime ep. 2; Bubbleblabber) and Arata refuses every advance, but the framing keeps the romance alive and the flash-forwards promise a marriage.
delivery.note: The family message is stated in sibling meetings and arc endings; the romance is carried by fan service and teasing rather than argued.

personified.ideology: Family is chosen and must be protected
Sibling bond as identity; incest as taboo
Parental love that hides hard truths

103036.heading: The Story of Our Unlikely Love
103036.label: From summaries
103036.life_message: Looking past rumors to who someone really is, and being honest about your own feelings, opens the way to love; kindness can draw out kindness in a person others have written off.

delivery.evidence: The message about rumor and kindness is carried by the romance and the tournament scene (Tokyopop; Kodansha blurb).
delivery.note: A two-volume romance with little room for argument; the story does not question the hero's pushiness (MyAnimeList reviews).

personified.ideology: Kindness and duty; trouble saying no

103036.dominant: No strong worldview; light Expressive individualism (refusing to conform) and Classical virtue ethics (kindness and effort).

168337.heading: The Strongest Evolutionary Necromancer
168337.label: From summaries
168337.life_message: A person is not bound by the role he was written into: with knowledge, discipline and allies, even a doomed side character can survive and grow strong.

delivery.evidence: Not enough plot detail was found to judge how rival views are treated (to verify).
delivery.note: A power-fantasy survival story; no message is stated in the sources opened beyond refusing a fated role.

personified.ideology: Self-made survival against a fixed fate

168337.dominant: Strength rules, Pagan/occult (necromancy as craft), Pragmatism, Existentialism (refusing a written fate).

99931.heading: The Strongest Sage with the Weakest Crest
99931.label: From summaries
99931.life_message: What you can do comes from true knowledge and hard practice, not from the label you were born with; the label itself may be a lie spread by those who want you weak, and the strong should use their power to protect people.

content.framing: Endorsed (heroic defense against demons and monsters)

delivery.evidence: The anti-prejudice point is made by Mathias proving his crest in battle, not by argument; ANN's anime review says the show is about how great Mathias is.
delivery.note: Those who scorn his crest, and the demons, are proven wrong rather than argued with.

personified.ideology: Skill and true knowledge over birth label

99931.dominant: Pragmatism, Traditionalism (recovering lost knowledge), Strength rules (explored), Pagan/occult (magic as craft).

100052.heading: The Summer of You
100052.label: From summaries
100052.life_message: Honest feelings, spoken without pressure and received with kindness, can turn a friendship into something deeper; real love respects the other person's pace.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: No character in sources opened argues against the romance, though ANN notes a largely homophobic background world; the message is carried by the boys' reactions and the summer trips (But Why Tho?; Paddylast Inc.).
delivery.note: The outlook on same-sex love is assumed rather than argued: acceptance is shown as the natural response.

personified.ideology: Honest love that asks nothing in return
Open acceptance; discovering one's own feelings

100052.dominant: Expressive individualism, Progressivism (affirming same-sex love), Secular humanism.

104203.heading: The Summer With You
104203.label: From summaries
104203.life_message: Love grows by learning to say what you feel: two young men who already love each other learn patience, consent and honesty as the relationship deepens.

delivery.evidence: No speeches; the relationship's values come through small scenes (the lost child, the kiss request, the drunk night) (Goodreads blog; Anime UK News).
delivery.note: A quiet slice-of-life romance that assumes the couple's love rather than arguing for it.

104203.dominant: Expressive individualism (choosing one's own love), Progressivism (an ordinary, affirmed gay couple), Liberalism (consent).

117620.heading: The Summer You Were There
117620.label: From summaries
117620.life_message: Even someone who has hurt others and wants to disappear is worth saving; honest apology, love and the people who stay can carry you through, and the meaning of time with someone lies in what it gave you, not in how long it lasted.

delivery.evidence: Carried by the romance and the illness plot; Kaori states her reason (she wanted to save Shizuku) at the aquarium (v6; Okazu); no reviewer comments on preachiness.
delivery.note: Living after loss and repairing harm are shown through events and a few honest confessions rather than lectures.

personified.ideology: Live and love fully in the time you have
Forgiveness is not owed but can be offered

117620.dominant: Existentialism (meaning within a limited time), Classical virtue ethics (accountability and apology), Communitarianism (the people who stay).

34625.heading: The Summit of the Gods
34625.label: From summaries
34625.life_message: A person can give his whole life to one hard, worthy summit, and the meaning lies in the giving everything, not in fame or even in coming home; but the cost falls on everyone who loves him, and even the most solitary climber is saved, and saves others, through another person.

delivery.evidence: The question of why people climb recurs through Habu's life and Mallory's famous answer (ANN); Dacey finds the narrator over-explains (Manga Bookshelf).
delivery.note: Rival climbers, Ryōko's waiting and the toll on families are shown seriously beside Habu's obsession; the story does not lecture.

personified.ideology: The ordinary man searching for meaning
A former Gurkha who wants to serve Nepal

34625.dominant: Existentialism, Expressive individualism (explored), Stoicism and Classical virtue ethics (endurance, courage).

97207.heading: The Two Faces of Misaki Hoshino.
97207.label: From summaries
97207.life_message: Who you are without the mask is worth showing, and standing up for others matters more than fitting in; the ending suggests growing up can also mean letting go.

delivery.evidence: The anti-bystander theme is stated once, loudly, in Kobayakawa's outburst (Japanese Wikipedia); elsewhere it is carried by side-character arcs, and even the bullies get backstories.
delivery.note: A school drama-comedy with a stated social point, carried mostly through character episodes.

personified.ideology: Strike first so you are not the target

97207.dominant: Expressive individualism (the bare face), Communitarianism (friends who stand together), Existentialism (choosing to be seen).

121204.heading: The Unrivaled Reincarnated Sage of Another World ~The Strongest in Another World Through Game Knowledges~
121204.label: From summaries
121204.life_message: Knowledge is strength meant to be shared and used well: careful study and humility can lift up people others overlook and defeat those who hoard and twist knowledge for themselves.

delivery.evidence: Villains are simply corrupt or cruel (the vol. 5 blurb has Georgis twisting knowledge to line his own pockets; the vol. 14 blurb calls an enemy general cruel); the message is carried by Eld's choices, not speeches.
delivery.note: A power-fantasy adventure; its values (humility, sharing knowledge, justice) are shown in action.

personified.ideology: Hoarding and twisting knowledge for power

121204.dominant: Pragmatism (game knowledge and careful planning); Classical virtue ethics (humility, prudence, courage); Might makes right (explored in a power fantasy).

100693.heading: The Unwanted Undead Adventurer
100693.label: From summaries
100693.life_message: Steady effort, kindness to the people around you and loyal friends can carry a person through even the loss of a human body; who you are is shown by how you treat others, not by what you look like.

content.framing: Neutral (monster combat); cruelty by humans condemned

delivery.evidence: Rentt's goodness shows in his actions while his narration undersells him; Gaffney notes the gap between his self-image and how others see him. Villains are few and flat (the slave traders, an arrogant exam party).
delivery.note: Summaries show the perseverance theme carried by step-by-step progress, not speeches.

100693.dominant: Classical virtue ethics, Communitarianism, Existentialism ("Existential Evolution"), Pragmatism.

126361.heading: The Villainess' Butler: Death Flag Destroyer at Your Service
126361.label: From summaries
126361.life_message: Loyal care and a good upbringing can change a fate that seems already written; you need not play the part others scripted for you.

delivery.evidence: The message is carried by Cyril's choices and Sophia's growth, not by speeches (publisher blurbs); the heroine and rivals are not villains in the blurbs.
delivery.note: A light romance whose values (diligence, loyalty, kindness) show through the plot.

personified.ideology: Faithful service and foresight can change fate

126361.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (raising a good person), Traditionalism (master and servant, noble duty), Existentialism (refusing a scripted fate).

55250.heading: The Voynich Hotel
55250.label: From summaries
55250.life_message: Broken, guilty and very odd people can still find love and a home among each other, though the past and death are never far away.

content.framing: Mixed: sex jokes played for comedy; the adult-and-witch romance endorsed
Mixed: addiction shown with costs, also played for laughs

delivery.evidence: No character lectures; the story moves through short black-comedy episodes. Hired killers and greedy characters are cartoonish, while the misfits get sympathy.
delivery.note: Meaning comes through accumulation of small stories (AniList reviews describe an anthology-like structure).

personified.ideology: A quiet man fleeing his past
Greed bought with a demon pact

55250.dominant: Absurdism (surreal black comedy), Pagan/occult (witches and demons), Communitarianism (found family), Postmodernism (pastiche).

101233.heading: The Way of the Househusband
101233.label: From summaries
101233.life_message: A good life is a quiet, devoted one: you can leave a violent past behind, and caring for your home and your spouse deserves the same skill, pride and seriousness as any job.

delivery.evidence: The message is in the premise and running gags rather than speeches; ex-yakuza who want Tatsu back are treated with affection, not contempt. CBR notes a rare stated line about not protecting what matters through violence.
delivery.note: Episodic gag structure: each chapter makes the same point in a new way.

personified.ideology: A changed life of quiet devotion
Career and passion in an equal marriage

101233.dominant: Communitarianism, Classical virtue ethics, Pacifism / nonviolence, Progressivism (explored).

118985.heading: The Weakest Tamer Began a Journey to Pick Up Trash
118985.label: From summaries
118985.life_message: Your worth is not your rank: a child cast out as worthless survives by thrift, honest work and kindness to weak creatures, and learns that trustworthy people matter more than any place.

content.framing: Condemned (abuse, murder, kidnapping); neutral (hunting and monster fights)

content.frequency: Heavy at the start, then recurring as trauma

content.framing: Shown as necessity; adults worry about it

delivery.evidence: The headman is drawn as petty and self-destroying (ch. 12); the adults state the message openly when Ivy reveals she is starless and they tell her the stars mean nothing (anime ep. 12; Wikipedia on Oght).
delivery.note: The anti-prejudice message is mostly shown through Ivy's struggle and the kindness she meets, but the villains are one-sided and the moral is spoken aloud near the arc's end.

personified.ideology: Worth beyond rank; honest work and kindness
Status by stars; superstition as power
Noble privilege used for profit and crime

118985.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (thrift, honesty, courage), Communitarianism (found family of protectors), Critical theory (rank-based discrimination critiqued), Pragmatism (resourcefulness).

100109.heading: The Witch and the Beast
100109.label: From summaries
100109.life_message: Judge people by what they do, not by their blood or reputation: power, whether a witch's or a church's, corrupts when it is used on the helpless, and hatred has to be tempered by trust.

content.framing: Shown with consequences; villains' cruelty condemned
Mixed: curse-breaking kisses as a power move

delivery.evidence: Each case shows prejudice and abused power through plot twists (a beloved witch who is a killer, a hated witch who is innocent); villains like Ione and Dornez get backstories that explain them; the Church has both good and bad members (fan wiki).
delivery.note: The message is shown case by case rather than stated, though Ashaf voices it at times.

personified.ideology: Power for the Church at any cost

100109.dominant: Pagan/occult (a world built on magic and curses), Might makes right (critiqued), Collectivism/authoritarianism (critiqued, in the Church's Executioners).

174233.heading: The Witch and the Mercenary
174233.label: From summaries
174233.life_message: Two people the world treats as disposable earn a place to live by keeping their word to each other; people should be judged by what they do, not by what they are.

content.framing: Neutral (professional combat shown as competence); persecution and cruelty condemned

delivery.evidence: Zig's neutrality and Siasha's wish for peace are shown through choices and contracts; the Old Continent's fear and the new continent's distrust are both shown from the inside; the Claritist villain's treatment is known only from blurbs.
delivery.note: The theme of prejudice is carried by the role reversal between the two continents rather than by speeches (Miyagi, K Manga).

personified.ideology: The right to live in peace
Old loyalties; the witch as enemy

174233.dominant: Pragmatism, Duty ethics (keeping one's word), Existentialism; Might makes right explored; prejudice critiqued.

107603.heading: The World's Finest Assassin Gets Reincarnated in Another World as an Aristocrat
107603.label: From summaries
107603.life_message: Skill, preparation and loyalty, used to protect others, can justify killing the wicked, and a second life should be lived for love and happiness rather than as someone else's tool.

content.framing: Endorsed (killing the guilty presented as professional and just)

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)
content.framing: Mixed: sexual exploitation condemned; fan service and harem endorsed

delivery.evidence: Lugh explains his reasoning in narration, and the goddess states the mission (Wikipedia); the target, Epona, is drawn sympathetically and the goddess is questioned, but the traffickers and corrupt nobles are simple villains.
delivery.note: The justification for killing is built into the premise rather than argued, though Lugh investigates whether targets deserve death (anime ep. 9).

personified.ideology: Ends justify means; skill in service of loved ones
Save the world at any cost

107603.dominant: Utilitarianism (explored), Pragmatism, Expressive individualism, Bushido / honor code (European form).

101734.heading: The World's Strongest Rearguard: Labyrinth Country's Novice Seeker
101734.label: From summaries
101734.life_message: Supporting others from behind, with care and teamwork, is real strength, and people the world treats as property are worth restoring.

content.framing: Neutral (played as comedy); villains' threats condemned (to verify)
Mixed: slavery accepted as the setting; the hero treats Theresia as a person

delivery.evidence: Villains (Bergen's group, Kyouka's first party, Beyond Liberty) are simple bad actors; the value of support and teamwork is stated by characters and blurbs (Yen Press vol. 1).
delivery.note: The message about supporting others is built into the hero's class and shown through battles rather than lectures.

101734.dominant: Communitarianism (teamwork), Classical virtue ethics (humble service and courage), Hedonism (harem fan service, explored), Pagan/occult (Hidden Gods and devotion).

99775.heading: The Wrong Way to Use Healing Magic
99775.label: From summaries
99775.life_message: Saving lives is as heroic as fighting, and hard discipline can make an ordinary person strong enough to protect and heal others, even enemies.

content.framing: Shown with consequences (deaths mourned); training violence played as comedy

delivery.evidence: The healer-as-hero theme is carried by training comedy and battle rescues; the view that healers are weak is voiced by the Luqvist students and disproved in a duel; Siglis voices doubts about Rose's brutality and concedes her results (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The idea that healing is heroic is shown through action rather than lectures; Rose's backstory explains her harshness without condemning it.

personified.ideology: Saving lives is as heroic as fighting
Harsh discipline makes the weak strong and keeps them alive
Loyalty forced by a military that took her from her family
Victory at any cost, even one's own soldiers

99775.dominant: Classical virtue ethics (character forged by discipline), Communitarianism (the Rescue Team), Stoicism (endurance), with a healer's mercy that edges toward nonviolence.

107896.heading: The Yakuza's Guide to Babysitting
107896.label: From summaries
107896.life_message: Even a violent man can change when he is trusted with a child's care; patience, love and found family matter more than reputation, and the past must be left behind.

content.framing: Mixed: protective violence shown with regret; cruelty condemned

delivery.evidence: The boss states the moral directly once (Kirishima is a babysitter and the Demon belongs in the past; anime ep. 11), but most of the message is carried by small domestic scenes. Rivals like Masaya get backstory; Mashiro and the kidnapper are flat.
delivery.note: A gentle comedy that turns serious at arc climaxes.

107896.dominant: Communitarianism (found family), Confucian ethics (loyalty in a family hierarchy), Bushido / honor code (the yakuza code, explored and softened).

119650.heading: There's No Freaking Way I'll be Your Lover! Unless...
119650.label: From summaries
119650.life_message: Dropping the mask you wear for others and saying honestly what you feel is how friendship and love become real; the story ends by letting Renako love two girls at once, with everyone's agreement.

content.framing: Mixed: Mai's forced advance at the end of vol. 1 is shown as wrong (Renako slaps her); much other pushiness is played as comedy; same-sex and three-way romance endorsed

delivery.evidence: The message about honesty and choosing your own relationships is shown through comedy and confessions; the story addresses the vol. 1 assault seriously only late in the volume (Gaffney) and otherwise treats pushiness lightly (ANN).
delivery.note: Light romantic comedy; no lectures. Its view of relationships is carried by who ends up happy.

personified.ideology: Safety in friendship, then honesty about love

119650.dominant: Expressive individualism, Progressivism (same-sex and agreed three-way romance), Hedonism (explored).

172729.heading: They Are Still Being Shaken This Morning
172729.label: From summaries
172729.life_message: Love grows by small acts of courage, and ordinary strangers who quietly wish others well make daily life kinder.

content.category: Sexuality and romance (incl. fan service, manga art vs anime)

delivery.evidence: Masuda wanted readers to feel "I know that feeling" with each character, from the teens to the onlookers (Web The Television); there is no lesson stated in sources opened.
delivery.note: Kindness among strangers and the value of small courage come through situations and jokes, not speeches.

172729.dominant: Communitarianism (strangers as a caring community), Classical virtue ethics (small courage).

80331.heading: This Art Club Has a Problem!
80331.label: From summaries
80331.life_message: Real friendships and honest feelings, even awkward ones, are worth more than perfect fantasies; talent grows best when it is shared with the people around you.

content.framing: Mixed: innocent crush endorsed; teasing gags played for comedy

delivery.evidence: Subaru's preference for fictional girls is gently mocked but never condemned; he is shown as talented and kind (Japanese Wikipedia).
delivery.note: An episodic comedy with no stated message; values come through Mizuki's point of view.

80331.dominant: Expressive individualism (explored), Communitarianism, Classical virtue ethics.

123777.heading: This Monster Wants to Eat Me
123777.label: From summaries
123777.life_message: Being truly seen and loved, even by someone who seems a monster, can slowly draw a grieving person back toward life; but love must reckon with the other person's own will, and saving someone is never simple.

content.framing: Explored with care; the death wish is never endorsed by the story

delivery.evidence: Hinako's view (death as relief), Shiori's (live, for my sake) and Miko's (live among people) are all given weight; Anime Feminist says the series offers no easy answers on whether saving her is right.
delivery.note: The message is carried by mood, imagery (drowning, the sea) and quiet character choices, not speeches.

personified.ideology: Possessive, protective love that overrides consent
Life within community; atonement through service
Bitterness at an unchosen immortal life

123777.dominant: Existentialism (the choice to live), Pagan/occult (yokai folklore), Nihilism (critiqued), Communitarianism (friends who will not let go).

97553.heading: Three Days of Happiness (Jumyou wo Kaitotte Moratta. Ichinen ni Tsuki, Ichimanen de.)
97553.label: From summaries
